foundation-iii/prime.s: A researcher at a teaching hospital plans a randomized trial of a new antihypertensive in adults. Before recruiting any participant, which step is mandatory?
o: Approval from an Institutional Review Board / Ethical Review Committee
Publication of the protocol in a journal
Verbal agreement from the head of department
Registration with the provincial health department only
foundation-iii/prime.e: Any research on human subjects requires prior ERC/IRB approval (Declaration of Helsinki); trial registration is also recommended but does not replace ethical approval.

foundation-iii/prime.s: A 45-year-old literate man is scheduled for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Which element is ESSENTIAL for valid informed consent?
o: Explanation of the procedure, its material risks and the reasonable alternatives
A statement that the surgeon guarantees a good outcome
Consent taken after premedication for convenience
Signature of a close relative as witness in all cases
Consent obtained by the house officer on the morning of surgery
foundation-iii/prime.e: Valid consent needs capacity, voluntariness and disclosure of nature, risks, benefits and alternatives; it must not be taken when the patient is sedated.

foundation-iii/prime.s: A new rapid test for typhoid is positive in 90 of 100 patients with culture-proven typhoid and negative in 80 of 100 patients without typhoid. What is the sensitivity of the test?
foundation-iii/prime.e: Sensitivity = true positives / all diseased = 90/100 = 90%. Specificity here = 80/100 = 80%.

foundation-iii/prime.s: In a trial, mortality is 10% in the control group and 6% in the treatment group. What is the number needed to treat (NNT) to prevent one death?

To study the association between smoking and bladder cancer, investigators select 200 patients with bladder cancer and 400 matched people without it and ask about past smoking. What type of study is this?
foundation-iii/prime.e: Starting from outcome (cases vs controls) and looking back at exposure defines a case-control study; the measure of association is the odds ratio.

foundation-iii/prime.s: A 28-year-old man tests HIV positive and refuses to tell his wife despite repeated counselling. What is the most appropriate next step for the doctor?
o: Inform him that the doctor may disclose to the spouse to protect her, and then do so if he still refuses
Maintain absolute confidentiality and take no further action
Report his name to the local media for public health
Disclose the result to his parents
foundation-iii/prime.e: Confidentiality may be breached when a specific, identifiable third party is at serious risk, after the patient has been counselled and told of the intended disclosure.

foundation-iii/prime.s: A pharmaceutical representative offers an intern an all-expenses-paid holiday in return for prescribing a particular brand. According to PMDC's Code of Ethics, what should the intern do?
o: Accept and prescribe the brand to half of the patients
Decline the offer as it creates a conflict of interest
Accept but declare it to the head of department
Accept if the drug is effective
Accept only if the holiday is within Pakistan
foundation-iii/prime.e: PMDC's code prohibits accepting gifts or inducements that could influence prescribing; it is a conflict of interest regardless of disclosure.

foundation-iii/prime.s: A patient receives a wrong drug due to a look-alike label. There is no harm. What is the best action by the doctor?
o: Blame the nurse in front of the patient
Report the incident through the hospital incident reporting system and inform the patient
Say nothing because no harm occurred
foundation-iii/prime.e: Near-misses and no-harm errors should be reported (for system learning) and disclosed honestly; a blame-free, systems approach improves safety.

foundation-iii/prime.s: Which approach is recommended as the FIRST step in breaking bad news using the SPIKES protocol?
o: Giving the diagnosis immediately to avoid anxiety
Setting up the interview in a private place with adequate time
Assessing the patient's knowledge after giving the news
foundation-iii/prime.e: SPIKES: Setting, Perception, Invitation, Knowledge, Emotions (with Empathy), Strategy and Summary.

foundation-iii/prime.s: Which of the following provides the HIGHEST level of evidence for a therapeutic intervention?
o: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
Expert opinion of a senior professor
foundation-iii/prime.e: In the hierarchy of evidence, systematic reviews/meta-analyses of well-conducted RCTs sit at the top.

foundation-iii/medicine.s: A 60-year-old man with pneumonia has BP 82/50 mmHg despite 30 mL/kg crystalloid, and serum lactate 4.5 mmol/L. What is the next most appropriate step?
o: Start noradrenaline to target mean arterial pressure ≥65 mmHg
Start dopamine as the first-line vasopressor
Give another 3 L of normal saline rapidly before any vasopressor
Withhold antibiotics until blood culture results
foundation-iii/medicine.e: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: noradrenaline is the first-line vasopressor for fluid-refractory septic shock, targeting MAP ≥65 mmHg; antibiotics within 1 hour.

foundation-iii/medicine.s: A 35-year-old man has had fever for 4 weeks. Examination, CBC, urine, chest X-ray and blood cultures are unremarkable. In Pakistan, which infection is an important cause to exclude next?
o: Extrapulmonary (e.g., abdominal or lymph node) tuberculosis
foundation-iii/medicine.e: In endemic regions, TB is a leading infectious cause of pyrexia of unknown origin, along with enteric fever, brucellosis and abscesses.

foundation-iii/medicine.s: A 55-year-old man receiving chemotherapy for high-grade lymphoma develops oliguria. Labs: K+ 6.4 mmol/L, uric acid 14 mg/dL, phosphate raised, calcium low. What is the most likely diagnosis?
foundation-iii/medicine.e: Rapid tumour cell death causes hyperkalaemia, hyperuricaemia, hyperphosphataemia and secondary hypocalcaemia with AKI; prevention is hydration plus allopurinol/rasburicase.

foundation-iii/medicine.s: A patient on chemotherapy has temperature 38.6°C and absolute neutrophil count 0.3 × 10⁹/L. He is haemodynamically stable. What is the most appropriate initial management?
o: Start oral paracetamol and review in 24 hours
Wait for culture results before antibiotics
Take blood cultures and start empirical IV broad-spectrum antipseudomonal antibiotic (e.g., piperacillin–tazobactam) within 1 hour
foundation-iii/medicine.e: Febrile neutropenia is a medical emergency; empirical antipseudomonal beta-lactam should be started within 1 hour.

foundation-iii/medicine.s: A patient with metastatic cancer has pain uncontrolled on regular paracetamol and codeine. According to the WHO analgesic ladder, what is the next step?
o: Stop all analgesia and refer to psychiatry
Increase codeine to twice maximum dose
Switch to a strong opioid such as oral morphine, with laxative
Add a second weak opioid such as tramadol
foundation-iii/medicine.e: Step 3 of the WHO ladder: strong opioid ± non-opioid ± adjuvant. Laxatives should be co-prescribed; pethidine is not suitable for chronic pain.

foundation-iii/medicine.s: A 25-year-old woman develops stridor, urticaria and BP 70/40 mmHg minutes after IV ceftriaxone. What is the FIRST drug to give?
o: Intramuscular adrenaline 0.5 mg (0.5 mL of 1:1000) into the anterolateral thigh
foundation-iii/medicine.e: IM adrenaline is the first-line treatment for anaphylaxis; antihistamines and steroids are adjuncts. IV 1 mg bolus is for cardiac arrest only.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A 30-year-old man after a road traffic accident has pulse 125/min, BP 90/60 mmHg, respiratory rate 32/min and is anxious/confused. According to ATLS, what is the estimated class of haemorrhage?
foundation-iii/surgery.e: Class III: HR >120, fall in systolic BP, RR 30–40, confused; requires blood transfusion.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A motorcyclist is brought in unconscious with gurgling sounds and suspected cervical spine injury. What is the first priority?
o: Airway maintenance with cervical spine protection (jaw thrust, suction)
foundation-iii/surgery.e: ATLS primary survey order: A (airway with C-spine protection), B, C, D, E.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: After a stab wound to the chest, a patient has severe respiratory distress, tracheal deviation to the left, absent breath sounds on the right and distended neck veins. What is the immediate management?
o: Needle/finger decompression in the 4th/5th intercostal space anterior to mid-axillary line (or 2nd ICS midclavicular), followed by chest drain
foundation-iii/surgery.e: Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis requiring immediate decompression before imaging; ATLS 10th ed. recommends the 4th/5th ICS anterior to the mid-axillary line in adults.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A 70-kg man has partial and full-thickness burns covering both upper limbs completely and the front of the trunk. Using the rule of nines, what is the total burn surface area?
foundation-iii/surgery.e: Each upper limb = 9% (18%) plus anterior trunk = 18%; total 36%.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: Using the Parkland formula, how much Ringer's lactate should a 60-kg adult with 30% TBSA burns receive in the first 8 hours from the time of burn?
foundation-iii/surgery.e: Parkland: 4 mL × kg × %TBSA = 4 × 60 × 30 = 7200 mL in 24 h; half (3600 mL) in the first 8 hours from the time of injury.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A 50-year-old man has a laparotomy wound that failed to heal and later opened. Which factor most commonly impairs wound healing?
foundation-iii/surgery.e: Infection is the commonest local cause of impaired healing and wound dehiscence; systemic factors include malnutrition, diabetes, steroids and jaundice.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A patient develops a wound infection 5 days after an open appendicectomy for perforated appendicitis. Such a wound is classified as:
foundation-iii/surgery.e: Surgery with pus or perforated viscus is a dirty wound (class IV), with SSI risk up to 40%.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A farmer has a deep, soil-contaminated wound on his foot. He has never been vaccinated against tetanus. What is the correct prophylaxis?
o: No prophylaxis needed if wound is cleaned
Tetanus toxoid course plus human tetanus immunoglobulin, with wound debridement
foundation-iii/surgery.e: Tetanus-prone wound in a non-immunized person needs both active (toxoid) and passive (TIG) immunization, plus thorough debridement.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A patient with prolonged vomiting from gastric outlet obstruction is most likely to have which biochemical abnormality?
o: Hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis with paradoxical aciduria
foundation-iii/surgery.e: Loss of HCl causes alkalosis; renal potassium loss and later H+ excretion in exchange for Na+ causes paradoxical aciduria. Treat with normal saline plus KCl.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A patient with a high-output enterocutaneous fistula has a non-functioning gut expected for more than 2 weeks. What is the best nutritional route?
o: Total parenteral nutrition via a central line
foundation-iii/surgery.e: When the GI tract cannot be used for a prolonged period, TPN is indicated; enteral is preferred whenever the gut works.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A 65-year-old man on aspirin and clopidogrel after coronary stenting 2 months ago needs elective inguinal hernia repair. What is the best plan?
o: Stop both drugs today and operate tomorrow
Defer the elective surgery until dual antiplatelet therapy is completed
Operate on dual antiplatelets under general anaesthesia without discussion
foundation-iii/surgery.e: Stopping DAPT early after stenting risks stent thrombosis; elective surgery should be postponed (at least 6 months after DES) with cardiology input.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A 55-year-old woman with well-controlled hypertension and type 2 diabetes without end-organ damage is posted for surgery. What is her ASA physical status?
foundation-iii/surgery.e: ASA II = mild systemic disease without substantive functional limitation (well-controlled HTN/DM).

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A 50-year-old has a 3 cm hard, painless lump in the neck. Which is the preferred initial investigation for tissue diagnosis?
o: Excision biopsy of the node immediately
foundation-iii/surgery.e: FNAC is first-line; excision biopsy of a neck node before ENT evaluation (to exclude a head–neck squamous primary) is avoided. Excision is needed if lymphoma is suspected.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A 25-year-old man has a painless testicular mass. Which tumour marker pair is most useful?
foundation-iii/surgery.e: AFP, β-hCG and LDH are the markers for germ cell tumours of the testis (seminoma does not raise AFP).

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A 68-year-old obese woman is scheduled for total hip replacement. What is the most appropriate thromboprophylaxis?
o: IV unfractionated heparin infusion at treatment dose
Aspirin 75 mg only on the day of surgery
No prophylaxis because she will mobilize
Low-molecular-weight heparin plus mechanical prophylaxis (stockings/intermittent pneumatic compression)
foundation-iii/surgery.e: Major orthopaedic surgery is very high risk for VTE; pharmacological (LMWH/DOAC) plus mechanical prophylaxis is recommended.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: Ten minutes into a blood transfusion, a patient develops fever, loin pain, hypotension and dark urine. What is the most likely cause?
o: Acute haemolytic transfusion reaction due to ABO incompatibility
foundation-iii/surgery.e: ABO incompatibility causes intravascular haemolysis within minutes; stop the transfusion immediately, keep IV access, recheck identity and send samples.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: What is the maximum safe dose of plain lignocaine (without adrenaline) for infiltration in a healthy adult?
foundation-iii/surgery.e: Plain lignocaine 3 mg/kg (max ~200 mg); with adrenaline 7 mg/kg (max ~500 mg).

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A 35-year-old diabetic has a painful, fluctuant 4 cm swelling on the buttock with overlying erythema. What is the management of choice?
o: Hot compresses and review in 1 week
Incision and drainage with breaking of loculi and send pus for culture
foundation-iii/surgery.e: "Ubi pus, ibi evacua" — fluctuant abscess requires drainage; control blood sugar. Antibiotics are adjuncts for cellulitis or systemic features.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A diabetic man has rapidly spreading painful erythema of the thigh with crepitus, bullae and pain out of proportion. What is the definitive management?
o: Urgent radical surgical debridement plus broad-spectrum IV antibiotics
Hyperbaric oxygen as the primary treatment
IV antibiotics and observe for 48 hours
foundation-iii/surgery.e: Necrotizing soft tissue infection is a surgical emergency; early aggressive debridement is life-saving.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: A patient develops fever on day 5 after laparotomy, with a red, tender, discharging wound. What is the most likely cause?
foundation-iii/surgery.e: The "5 Ws": Wind (atelectasis, day 1–2), Water (UTI, day 3–5), Wound (day 5–7), Walking (DVT, day 7–10), Wonder drugs.

foundation-iii/surgery.s: During general anaesthesia with succinylcholine and sevoflurane, a patient develops rising end-tidal CO₂, tachycardia, muscle rigidity and hyperthermia. What is the specific treatment?
o: IV dantrolene and stopping the triggering agents
foundation-iii/surgery.e: Malignant hyperthermia (RYR1 mutation) is treated with dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg, stopping volatile agents, cooling and treating hyperkalaemia.

foundation-iii/psychiatry.s: A 70-year-old man with delirium refuses urgent treatment for sepsis. Which is the key element in assessing decision-making capacity?
o: Ability to understand, retain, weigh information and communicate a decision
Whether he agrees with the doctor
The opinion of his family members
foundation-iii/psychiatry.e: Capacity is decision-specific and assessed functionally; disagreement with doctors does not by itself indicate incapacity.

foundation-iii/psychiatry.s: A 32-year-old woman has visited multiple doctors for 2 years with abdominal pain, headaches and back pain. All investigations are normal. She is persistently worried about her symptoms. What is the best management approach?
o: Repeat all investigations at each visit
Tell her the symptoms are imaginary
Regular scheduled visits with one doctor, acknowledging symptoms, limiting unnecessary investigations, and CBT
foundation-iii/psychiatry.e: Somatic symptom disorder management involves a consistent physician, scheduled appointments, avoiding over-investigation, and CBT/SSRIs when indicated.

foundation-iii/psychiatry.s: A 78-year-old man becomes acutely confused and agitated on the second night after hip surgery, with fluctuating attention. What is the first step in management?
o: Identify and treat the underlying cause (e.g., infection, hypoxia, drugs, urinary retention) and use non-pharmacological measures
Physically restrain and sedate as first line
foundation-iii/psychiatry.e: Delirium is an acute confusional state with an underlying cause; low-dose haloperidol is only for severe distress or danger. Benzodiazepines worsen delirium (except in alcohol withdrawal).

foundation-iii/psychiatry.s: A 45-year-old man admitted for surgery develops tremors, sweating, visual hallucinations and disorientation 48–72 hours after admission. What is the drug of choice?
o: Benzodiazepine (e.g., chlordiazepoxide or diazepam) plus IV thiamine
foundation-iii/psychiatry.e: Delirium tremens is treated with benzodiazepines; thiamine is given before glucose to prevent Wernicke's encephalopathy.

foundation-iii/psychiatry.s: A 40-year-old man whose wife died 3 weeks ago has sadness, crying spells and occasional sleep difficulty but continues working and has no suicidal ideas. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Supportive counselling and reassurance that this is a normal grief reaction
foundation-iii/psychiatry.e: Normal bereavement does not require medication; follow up to detect prolonged grief disorder or major depression.

foundation-iii/psychiatry.s: A young man is brought unconscious with respiratory rate 6/min and pinpoint pupils. What is the immediate drug treatment?
foundation-iii/psychiatry.e: Opioid toxicity (coma, miosis, respiratory depression) is reversed with naloxone; short half-life may require repeated doses or infusion.

foundation-iii/paediatrics.s: A newborn has upslanting palpebral fissures, flat facial profile, single palmar crease and hypotonia. Which cardiac lesion is most characteristic of this condition?
foundation-iii/paediatrics.e: Down syndrome (trisomy 21) is associated with AVSD (endocardial cushion defect), VSD and ASD; echocardiography is recommended for all.

foundation-iii/paediatrics.s: A boy has progressive proximal muscle weakness, Gowers' sign and calf pseudohypertrophy. His maternal uncle had similar disease. What is the mode of inheritance?
foundation-iii/paediatrics.e: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is X-linked recessive (dystrophin gene); mothers are carriers.

foundation-iii/paediatrics.s: According to the EPI schedule of Pakistan, which vaccines are given at birth?
o: BCG, OPV-0 and Hepatitis B birth dose
foundation-iii/paediatrics.e: EPI Pakistan gives BCG, OPV-0 and hepatitis B at birth; the 6-, 10- and 14-week visits add OPV, pentavalent/hexavalent, PCV (and rotavirus at 6 and 10 weeks). Check the current provincial EPI schedule as combination vaccines are being updated.

foundation-iii/paediatrics.s: A 3-day-old baby born after prolonged rupture of membranes is lethargic, feeding poorly and has temperature instability. What is the most appropriate empirical antibiotic regimen?
o: IV ampicillin plus gentamicin after blood culture
IV ceftriaxone alone in all neonates
foundation-iii/paediatrics.e: Early-onset neonatal sepsis (GBS, E. coli, Listeria) is treated with ampicillin plus an aminoglycoside. Ceftriaxone is avoided in jaundiced neonates (bilirubin displacement).

foundation-iii/paediatrics.s: Using the Holliday–Segar formula, what is the daily maintenance fluid requirement of a 25-kg child?
foundation-iii/paediatrics.e: 100 mL/kg for first 10 kg (1000) + 50 mL/kg for next 10 kg (500) + 20 mL/kg for remaining 5 kg (100) = 1600 mL/day.

foundation-iii/paediatrics.s: A 6-month-old infant has multiple posterior rib fractures of different ages and retinal haemorrhages. Parents say he rolled off a sofa. What is the most likely diagnosis?
foundation-iii/paediatrics.e: Posterior rib fractures of varying ages and retinal haemorrhages in a non-mobile infant are highly specific for abusive trauma; safeguarding procedures must be followed.

foundation-iii/radiology.s: Which imaging modality exposes the patient to the HIGHEST ionizing radiation dose?
o: CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis
foundation-iii/radiology.e: CT abdomen–pelvis ≈ 10 mSv (~500 chest X-rays). Ultrasound and MRI do not use ionizing radiation.

foundation-iii/radiology.s: A 26-year-old pregnant woman at 10 weeks has right iliac fossa pain. Which is the preferred first imaging investigation?
foundation-iii/radiology.e: Ultrasound is first-line in pregnancy (no ionizing radiation); MRI without gadolinium is the next step if ultrasound is inconclusive.

foundation-iii/radiology.s: Before a contrast-enhanced CT, which is the most important measure to reduce contrast-associated nephropathy in a patient with eGFR 35 mL/min/1.73m²?
o: Adequate IV hydration with isotonic saline and using the minimum contrast dose
Doubling the contrast dose for better images
foundation-iii/radiology.e: Risk reduction: confirm indication, isotonic IV fluids, lowest dose of low/iso-osmolar contrast, and hold nephrotoxins; metformin may need withholding.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 1-year-old boy from Peshawar has severe pallor, hepatosplenomegaly, frontal bossing and Hb 5 g/dL with microcytic hypochromic indices and target cells. What investigation confirms the diagnosis?
o: Haemoglobin electrophoresis/HPLC showing markedly raised HbF with absent or reduced HbA
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: β-thalassaemia major presents at 6–12 months as HbF falls; HPLC shows high HbF and absent/low HbA.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 7-year-old transfusion-dependent thalassaemia child has serum ferritin 2800 ng/mL. Which is the preferred oral iron chelator?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Deferasirox is a once-daily oral chelator; desferrioxamine is given as subcutaneous infusion; deferiprone is another oral option (monitor for agranulocytosis).

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 15-month-old child who drinks over 1 litre of cow's milk daily has pallor and Hb 7.5 g/dL, MCV 58 fL, low ferritin and raised RDW. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Oral elemental iron 3–6 mg/kg/day, reduce cow's milk intake and dietary counselling
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Nutritional iron deficiency is treated with oral iron; response is seen as a reticulocyte rise in 5–10 days; continue for 2–3 months after Hb normalises.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A child has Hb 11 g/dL, MCV 62 fL, RBC count 6.2 × 10¹²/L and normal ferritin. The Mentzer index is about 10. What is the most likely diagnosis?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Mentzer index (MCV/RBC) <13 suggests thalassaemia trait; >13 suggests iron deficiency. Confirm with HbA2 >3.5% on HPLC.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 2-year-old boy has a swollen, painful knee after a minor fall. His maternal uncle had a similar problem. Platelets and PT are normal; APTT is prolonged. What is the most likely deficiency?
o: Von Willebrand factor with low platelets
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Haemophilia A (X-linked) causes haemarthroses with isolated prolonged APTT; treat with factor VIII concentrate (or emicizumab prophylaxis).

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 4-year-old girl develops widespread petechiae and bruises 2 weeks after a viral illness. She is well otherwise, with no hepatosplenomegaly. Platelets are 12 × 10⁹/L; Hb and WBC are normal. There is no mucosal bleeding. What is the best management?
o: Observation with parental counselling and avoidance of NSAIDs/contact sports
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Childhood ITP is usually self-limiting; with only skin bleeding, watchful waiting is recommended. IVIG or short-course steroids are for significant bleeding.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 5-year-old boy has fever, bone pain, pallor, petechiae and hepatosplenomegaly for 3 weeks. Blood film shows blasts. What is the most important investigation to establish the diagnosis?
o: Bone marrow aspirate with immunophenotyping (flow cytometry)
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: ALL diagnosis requires ≥20% (usually >25%) lymphoblasts in marrow with immunophenotyping, cytogenetics and CSF assessment for staging.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: Which feature indicates a GOOD prognosis in childhood acute lymphoblastic leukaemia?
o: Age 1–10 years with WBC <50 × 10⁹/L at diagnosis
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Favourable: age 1–10, WBC <50,000, hyperdiploidy, t(12;21), rapid early response (low MRD).

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A child with T-cell ALL and WBC 250 × 10⁹/L is about to begin induction. Which drug is best to prevent hyperuricaemia in high-risk tumour lysis?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Rasburicase (recombinant urate oxidase) rapidly lowers uric acid in high-risk TLS; contraindicated in G6PD deficiency.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 3-year-old boy develops dark urine, pallor and jaundice 2 days after being treated with primaquine. Blood film shows bite cells and Heinz bodies. What is the most likely diagnosis?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Oxidant drugs (primaquine, dapsone, sulfonamides), fava beans and infections trigger intravascular haemolysis in G6PD deficiency (X-linked).

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 6-year-old has intermittent jaundice, splenomegaly and gallstones. Family history is positive. Blood film shows spherocytes, MCHC is raised and direct Coombs test is negative. Which test confirms the diagnosis?
o: Eosin-5'-maleimide (EMA) binding flow cytometry (or osmotic fragility)
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: HS (autosomal dominant, spectrin/ankyrin defects) is confirmed by EMA binding test; splenectomy is deferred until after 6 years with vaccinations.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A child with sickle cell disease presents with sudden pallor, abdominal distension, massively enlarged spleen and Hb falling from 8 to 4 g/dL. What is the diagnosis?
o: Aplastic crisis due to parvovirus B19
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Splenic sequestration presents with rapid Hb fall, enlarging spleen and shock, with high reticulocytes; needs urgent transfusion. Aplastic crisis has low reticulocytes.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 9-year-old has pancytopenia, short stature, café-au-lait spots and absent thumbs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Fanconi anaemia: autosomal recessive DNA repair defect; chromosomal breakage test with diepoxybutane/mitomycin C confirms. Risk of AML and solid tumours.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 3-month-old infant has severe macrocytic anaemia with reticulocytopenia, normal WBC and platelets, and a triphalangeal thumb. What is the likely diagnosis?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: DBA is pure red cell aplasia presenting in infancy with macrocytosis, raised HbF and eADA; steroids are first-line after 1 year.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A baby born to an O Rh-negative mother becomes jaundiced within 12 hours of birth. Direct Coombs test on the baby is strongly positive. What is the most likely cause?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Jaundice within 24 hours is always pathological; strongly positive DCT with Rh-negative mother indicates Rh haemolytic disease.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: In a neonate with severe haemolytic disease, which blood is used for double-volume exchange transfusion?
o: O Rh-negative red cells suspended in AB plasma, cross-matched against mother's serum
Baby's own blood group Rh-positive whole blood
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: For Rh HDN, O Rh-negative cells (compatible with maternal antibodies) in AB plasma are used; double volume = 2 × 80–85 mL/kg.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 5-week-old exclusively breastfed baby born at home presents with intracranial haemorrhage. PT and APTT are both prolonged; platelets normal. What was the most likely preventable cause?
o: Omission of vitamin K prophylaxis at birth (late vitamin K deficiency bleeding)
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Late VKDB (2–12 weeks) occurs in breastfed babies not given IM vitamin K 1 mg at birth; often presents with intracranial bleeding.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: An infant of a diabetic mother has plethora, lethargy and venous haematocrit of 70%. He is symptomatic with poor feeding. What is the appropriate treatment?
o: Partial exchange transfusion with normal saline
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Symptomatic neonatal polycythaemia (venous Hct >65%) is treated with partial exchange transfusion using normal saline.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 9-month-old boy has recurrent bacterial pneumonias and otitis media since age 6 months. Tonsils and lymph nodes are absent. Serum immunoglobulins are all very low and B cells are absent. What is the diagnosis?
o: Severe combined immunodeficiency with normal B cells
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: BTK mutation stops B-cell maturation; infections begin after maternal IgG wanes (~6 months). Treated with lifelong IVIG.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A child has recurrent liver abscesses and lymphadenitis due to Staphylococcus aureus and Aspergillus. Which test is diagnostic?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: CGD (NADPH oxidase defect) causes infections with catalase-positive organisms; DHR test (replacing NBT test) shows absent oxidative burst.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A boy has eczema, recurrent infections and bleeding with small platelets. What is the diagnosis?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: WAS (X-linked, WASP gene): triad of eczema, thrombocytopenia with small platelets, recurrent infections; cure by HSCT.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A neonate with interrupted aortic arch develops hypocalcaemic seizures and has recurrent viral and fungal infections. Chest X-ray shows absent thymic shadow. What is the chromosomal defect?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: DiGeorge (CATCH-22): cardiac defects, abnormal facies, thymic hypoplasia, cleft palate, hypocalcaemia.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: An HIV-exposed infant born to a mother with HIV needs early diagnosis at 6 weeks of age. Which test is appropriate?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Maternal antibodies persist up to 18 months, so infant diagnosis requires virological (NAT) testing.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 3-year-old child has punched-out lytic skull lesions, seborrhoeic-like rash, exophthalmos and diabetes insipidus. What is the diagnosis?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: LCH shows CD1a/CD207 (langerin)-positive cells with Birbeck granules; the classic triad (Hand–Schüller–Christian) is lytic skull lesions, DI and exophthalmos.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 14-year-old boy has painless cervical lymphadenopathy, night sweats and weight loss. Lymph node biopsy shows Reed–Sternberg cells. Which markers are typically positive on these cells?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma RS cells express CD15 and CD30 and usually lack CD45 and CD20.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 7-year-old boy presents with a rapidly growing abdominal mass and intussusception. Biopsy shows a "starry sky" pattern. Which translocation is characteristic?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Burkitt lymphoma: MYC translocation t(8;14); very rapid growth with high risk of tumour lysis syndrome.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 10-month-old exclusively breastfed infant of a strict vegan mother has developmental regression, hypotonia, and macrocytic anaemia with hypersegmented neutrophils. What is the most likely deficiency?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Maternal B12 deficiency leads to infant B12 deficiency with neurological regression; treat with IM hydroxocobalamin.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 3-year-old child with pica has abdominal pain, irritability and microcytic anaemia. Blood film shows basophilic stippling. What is the most likely diagnosis?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Lead inhibits haem synthesis (ALA dehydratase, ferrochelatase) causing basophilic stippling; chelation with succimer/EDTA for high levels.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: In a child with severe anaemia and signs of heart failure, what is the appropriate way to give red cell transfusion?
o: Small-volume packed red cells (e.g., 5 mL/kg) slowly with IV furosemide
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: In decompensated severe anaemia, small aliquots of packed cells with diuretic prevent volume overload.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 13-year-old girl has heavy menstrual bleeding since menarche and frequent epistaxis. Platelet count and PT are normal; APTT slightly prolonged; bleeding time prolonged. What is the most likely diagnosis?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: vWD (commonest inherited bleeding disorder) causes mucocutaneous bleeding; mild type 1 responds to desmopressin (DDAVP) and tranexamic acid.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 2-year-old has recurrent fevers, mouth ulcers and gingivitis occurring every 21 days, each lasting 5 days, with neutrophils falling to near zero during episodes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: Cyclic neutropenia (ELANE mutation) has ~21-day cycles; G-CSF reduces episode severity.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A child with partial oculocutaneous albinism, recurrent pyogenic infections and peripheral neuropathy has giant granules in neutrophils. What is the diagnosis?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: CHS is due to LYST mutation (lysosomal trafficking); giant granules on smear; risk of haemophagocytic "accelerated phase".

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A neonate has delayed separation of the umbilical cord (at 5 weeks), omphalitis without pus, and persistent neutrophilia. What is the defect?
o: CD18 (β2 integrin) deficiency – leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: LAD-1: neutrophils cannot adhere and migrate, so infections without pus formation and marked leukocytosis.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 2-year-old has prolonged fever, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, ferritin 12,000 ng/mL, high triglycerides and low fibrinogen. What is the most likely diagnosis?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: HLH-2004 criteria include fever, splenomegaly, cytopenias, hypertriglyceridaemia/hypofibrinogenaemia, very high ferritin and haemophagocytosis. Visceral leishmaniasis and EBV can trigger it.

blood-iii/paediatrics.s: A 4-month-old has chronic diarrhoea, oral thrush, failure to thrive and Pneumocystis pneumonia. Lymphocyte count is very low. Which vaccine must be avoided?
blood-iii/paediatrics.e: In SCID, live vaccines (BCG, rotavirus, OPV, MMR) can cause disseminated infection; definitive treatment is HSCT.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 62-year-old man has Hb 9 g/dL, MCV 70 fL and ferritin 8 ng/mL. He has no GI symptoms. What is the most important next step?
o: Start oral iron and no further tests
Upper GI endoscopy and colonoscopy to exclude gastrointestinal malignancy
blood-iii/medicine.e: Iron deficiency in men and postmenopausal women warrants bidirectional endoscopy to exclude GI blood loss (e.g., colorectal cancer).

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 55-year-old woman has fatigue, glossitis, paraesthesia of the feet, loss of vibration sense and MCV 118 fL. Which antibody is most specific for the likely cause?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Anti-IF is highly specific (~50% sensitive) for pernicious anaemia; anti-parietal cell is sensitive but less specific.

blood-iii/medicine.s: In a patient with severe B12 deficiency and folate deficiency, why must B12 be replaced before or with folate?
o: Folate alone may precipitate or worsen subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord
blood-iii/medicine.e: Folate alone can correct the anaemia but allow neurological damage to progress; hypokalaemia can also occur early in treatment due to K+ uptake.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 50-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis has Hb 10 g/dL, MCV 80 fL, low serum iron, low TIBC and high ferritin. What is the diagnosis?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Hepcidin-mediated iron sequestration: low iron, low/normal TIBC, normal/high ferritin. IDA shows high TIBC and low ferritin.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 35-year-old woman with SLE has jaundice, anaemia, raised reticulocytes, spherocytes and positive direct antiglobulin test for IgG. What is the first-line treatment?
o: Keep warm and avoid cold exposure
blood-iii/medicine.e: Warm (IgG) AIHA responds to corticosteroids first; rituximab is second-line; splenectomy for refractory cases.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A patient recovering from Mycoplasma pneumonia develops acrocyanosis and haemolysis on exposure to cold. DAT is positive for C3d. What is the antibody class?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Cold agglutinins are IgM that bind at low temperatures and fix complement; avoidance of cold is key and steroids are ineffective.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old man has haemolytic anaemia, pancytopenia, dark morning urine and hepatic vein thrombosis. What is the diagnostic test?
o: Flow cytometry for CD55/CD59 (or FLAER) deficiency on blood cells
blood-iii/medicine.e: PNH (PIGA mutation) causes loss of GPI-anchored proteins; thrombosis is the leading cause of death. Eculizumab/ravulizumab block C5.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 25-year-old man has pancytopenia with no splenomegaly. Bone marrow trephine shows hypocellular marrow (<25%) replaced by fat, without abnormal cells. He has a matched sibling. What is the treatment of choice?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Severe aplastic anaemia in young patients with a matched sibling donor: HSCT. Others: ATG + ciclosporin + eltrombopag.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 45-year-old man has massive splenomegaly and WBC 180 × 10⁹/L with neutrophils and myelocytes and basophilia. What is the drug of choice?
blood-iii/medicine.e: CML (BCR-ABL1, Philadelphia chromosome) is treated with TKIs such as imatinib; hydroxyurea is only for initial cytoreduction.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old woman has bleeding gums, DIC and blasts containing Auer rods in bundles (faggot cells). Which drug should be started urgently?
blood-iii/medicine.e: APL (t(15;17), PML-RARA) is a medical emergency due to DIC; ATRA ± arsenic trioxide should be started on suspicion.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 70-year-old man has incidental lymphocytosis of 40 × 10⁹/L with smudge cells. He is asymptomatic, Binet stage A. What is the management?
o: Watch and wait with regular monitoring
blood-iii/medicine.e: Early-stage asymptomatic CLL does not benefit from early treatment; treat when active disease criteria develop (e.g., BTK inhibitors).

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 65-year-old man has back pain, anaemia, raised creatinine, calcium 12 mg/dL and a high total protein. Which investigation best supports the diagnosis?
o: Serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation and serum free light chains showing monoclonal protein
blood-iii/medicine.e: Myeloma: CRAB features; M-band on SPEP, free light chains, and ≥10% clonal plasma cells in marrow. Bone scans are usually negative (lytic lesions).

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 28-year-old woman has cervical and mediastinal lymphadenopathy with fevers and 12% weight loss. Spleen is not involved. What is her Ann Arbor stage?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Two nodal regions on the same side of the diaphragm = stage II; B symptoms (fever, night sweats, >10% weight loss in 6 months) = B.

blood-iii/medicine.s: Which regimen is standard first-line treatment for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Rituximab-based anthracycline chemotherapy is standard for DLBCL; ABVD is used for Hodgkin lymphoma.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 60-year-old man has aquagenic pruritus, plethora, splenomegaly and Hb 19.5 g/dL. Which mutation is found in about 95% of cases?
blood-iii/medicine.e: JAK2 V617F in ~95% of PV (exon 12 in most of the rest). Treatment: venesection to Hct <45%, aspirin, hydroxyurea if high risk.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 32-year-old woman has fever, confusion, severe thrombocytopenia, schistocytes on film, raised LDH and mild renal impairment. PT and APTT are normal. What is the urgent treatment?
blood-iii/medicine.e: TTP (ADAMTS13 deficiency) is a haematological emergency; platelet transfusion is avoided unless life-threatening bleeding.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A patient on unfractionated heparin for 7 days has platelets drop from 250 to 90 × 10⁹/L and develops a new DVT. What is the correct management?
o: Stop all heparin and start a non-heparin anticoagulant (e.g., argatroban or fondaparinux)
blood-iii/medicine.e: HIT is prothrombotic; stop heparin (including LMWH and flushes), use non-heparin anticoagulant; warfarin only once platelets recover.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A patient with septic shock has bleeding from cannula sites, low platelets, prolonged PT/APTT, low fibrinogen and high D-dimer. What is the cornerstone of management?
o: Give tranexamic acid as first line
Start high-dose heparin in all bleeding patients
Treat the underlying cause with supportive blood products for active bleeding
blood-iii/medicine.e: DIC is secondary; treat sepsis, and replace platelets/FFP/cryoprecipitate if bleeding or high risk.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A patient on warfarin has INR 8.5 with an intracranial haemorrhage. What is the most appropriate treatment?
o: Oral vitamin K only and recheck INR in 24 hours
Stop warfarin, give IV vitamin K 5–10 mg and four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate
blood-iii/medicine.e: Major bleeding on warfarin requires PCC (or FFP if unavailable) plus IV vitamin K. Protamine reverses heparin.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A patient with atrial fibrillation on dabigatran presents with life-threatening GI bleeding. Which is the specific reversal agent?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Idarucizumab is a monoclonal antibody fragment reversing dabigatran; andexanet alfa reverses factor Xa inhibitors.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 34-year-old woman has had a DVT and three first-trimester miscarriages. Lupus anticoagulant is positive on two occasions 12 weeks apart. What is the long-term anticoagulant of choice after thrombosis?
blood-iii/medicine.e: In thrombotic APS, warfarin is preferred; DOACs are inferior, especially in triple-positive APS. In pregnancy, LMWH plus aspirin is used.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 25-year-old with severe haemophilia A develops an inhibitor to factor VIII and presents with a bleed. Which agent is appropriate?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Inhibitors neutralize FVIII; bypassing agents (rFVIIa, FEIBA) treat bleeding; emicizumab is used for prophylaxis.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A patient is scheduled for elective splenectomy for refractory ITP. Which vaccinations should be given at least 2 weeks before surgery?
o: Pneumococcal, Haemophilus influenzae type b, meningococcal (ACWY and B) and annual influenza
blood-iii/medicine.e: Asplenic patients are at risk of overwhelming post-splenectomy infection by encapsulated organisms.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A patient on day 5 of dengue fever has abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, rising haematocrit with falling platelets and mild pleural effusion. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Admit and give carefully titrated IV isotonic crystalloids with haematocrit monitoring
blood-iii/medicine.e: Warning signs during the critical phase indicate plasma leakage; fluid therapy guided by Hct is key. Prophylactic platelets are not recommended; avoid NSAIDs.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A traveller returning from Karachi has fever, jaundice, confusion and Plasmodium falciparum parasitaemia of 8%. What is the treatment of choice?
o: IV quinine as first choice where artesunate is available
blood-iii/medicine.e: Severe falciparum malaria is treated with IV artesunate, followed by a full course of oral ACT.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 72-year-old man has refractory macrocytic anaemia and neutropenia. Film shows pseudo-Pelger–Huët cells; marrow shows dysplasia with 5% blasts and ring sideroblasts. What is the diagnosis?
blood-iii/medicine.e: MDS is clonal ineffective haematopoiesis in the elderly with dysplasia and <20% blasts; ≥20% indicates AML.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 55-year-old woman has platelet count 1100 × 10⁹/L on repeated testing, with erythromelalgia. Ferritin and CRP are normal. Which mutation is second most common after JAK2 in this condition?
blood-iii/medicine.e: ET mutations: JAK2 (~55%), CALR (~25%), MPL (~5%). Exclude reactive thrombocytosis and CML.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old man with fever and generalized lymphadenopathy is HIV positive. His CD4 count is 150 cells/mm³. According to WHO guidelines, what is the recommended first-line ART regimen for adults?
blood-iii/medicine.e: WHO recommends TLD as preferred first-line ART for all adults irrespective of CD4 count; cotrimoxazole prophylaxis for CD4 <200 (or <350 per settings).

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 25-year-old man has matted cervical lymph nodes with a discharging sinus and evening fever. What is the most likely diagnosis in Pakistan?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Matted nodes with caseation, cold abscess and sinus formation ("collar-stud abscess") are typical of TB; FNAC/biopsy with GeneXpert confirms.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 22-year-old woman develops DVT after starting the combined oral contraceptive pill. Her mother had a PE. Which is the most common inherited thrombophilia in Caucasians?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Factor V Leiden (activated protein C resistance) is the most common inherited thrombophilia; oestrogen-containing contraception should be avoided.

blood-iii/medicine.s: Within 6 hours of a transfusion, a patient develops acute hypoxia and bilateral pulmonary infiltrates with normal JVP and no fluid overload. What is the diagnosis?
blood-iii/medicine.e: TRALI is due to donor anti-HLA/HNA antibodies causing non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema; TACO has raised JVP, hypertension and responds to diuretics.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A patient with cirrhosis has splenomegaly, platelets 60 × 10⁹/L, WBC 3.0 × 10⁹/L and Hb 10 g/dL. Marrow is normocellular. What is the cause of the cytopenias?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Splenic pooling and destruction cause pancytopenia with a normal/hyperplastic marrow.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 68-year-old has massive splenomegaly, tear-drop cells and a leucoerythroblastic film. Bone marrow aspiration is a "dry tap". What is the diagnosis?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Marrow fibrosis causes dry tap, extramedullary haematopoiesis and dacrocytes; JAK2/CALR/MPL mutations are common; ruxolitinib for symptoms.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 50-year-old man has pancytopenia, splenomegaly and cells with cytoplasmic projections that are TRAP-positive. Which mutation is typical?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Hairy cell leukaemia: TRAP+, CD11c, CD25, CD103, annexin A1; BRAF V600E; cladribine is highly effective.

blood-iii/medicine.s: A 40-year-old has fatigue, gum hypertrophy, and blasts that are myeloperoxidase positive with monocytic features. What is the most likely FAB subtype?
blood-iii/medicine.e: Monocytic AML (M4/M5) characteristically infiltrates gums and skin; M3 causes DIC; M7 is megakaryoblastic.

blood-iii/gynaecology.s: A 28-week pregnant woman has Hb 8.5 g/dL, low ferritin and cannot tolerate oral iron. What is the most appropriate treatment?
o: Stop all iron and recheck in 4 weeks
blood-iii/gynaecology.e: Parenteral iron is recommended in the second/third trimester for intolerance or non-response to oral iron; transfusion is for severe anaemia near term or haemodynamic compromise.

blood-iii/gynaecology.s: A Rh-negative, non-sensitized primigravida has an uncomplicated pregnancy. When is routine antenatal anti-D prophylaxis recommended?
o: At 28 weeks (single or two-dose regimen) and within 72 hours after delivery of a Rh-positive baby
blood-iii/gynaecology.e: RAADP at 28 weeks (±34 weeks) plus postnatal anti-D within 72 hours (dose guided by Kleihauer test).

blood-iii/gynaecology.s: A 35-year-old woman with previous unprovoked DVT becomes pregnant. What is the recommended thromboprophylaxis?
o: Prophylactic LMWH antenatally throughout pregnancy and for 6 weeks postpartum
blood-iii/gynaecology.e: Previous unprovoked VTE is high risk; LMWH from early pregnancy until 6 weeks postpartum. Warfarin is teratogenic and DOACs are avoided in pregnancy.

blood-iii/gynaecology.s: A 34-week pregnant woman with pre-eclampsia has epigastric pain, platelets 70 × 10⁹/L, raised ALT and haemolysis with raised LDH. What is the definitive management?
o: Stabilise (BP control, magnesium sulphate) and expedite delivery
blood-iii/gynaecology.e: HELLP (Haemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelets) is a severe form of pre-eclampsia; delivery is definitive.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 40-year-old woman has symmetrical pain and swelling of the MCP and PIP joints with morning stiffness lasting 2 hours for 3 months. Which antibody is most specific for her likely diagnosis?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Anti-CCP has ~95% specificity for RA and predicts erosive disease; RF is less specific.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A newly diagnosed patient with active rheumatoid arthritis has no contraindications. What is the first-line conventional DMARD?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Methotrexate is the anchor DMARD (EULAR); short-term bridging steroids may be used; biologics after csDMARD failure.

msk-iii/medicine.s: Which baseline and monitoring investigations are essential for a patient starting methotrexate?
o: Serum uric acid and urine microscopy only
CBC, liver function tests, renal function and chest X-ray at baseline
msk-iii/medicine.e: Methotrexate can cause myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity and pneumonitis; it is renally excreted. Hydroxychloroquine requires retinal screening.

msk-iii/medicine.s: Before starting a TNF-alpha inhibitor in a patient from Pakistan, which infection must be screened for?
o: Latent tuberculosis (IGRA/tuberculin test and chest X-ray)
msk-iii/medicine.e: Anti-TNF therapy can reactivate latent TB; also screen for hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 60-year-old with long-standing seropositive RA has splenomegaly, neutropenia and recurrent infections. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Felty syndrome: RA + splenomegaly + neutropenia. Caplan syndrome: RA + pneumoconiosis with lung nodules.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 25-year-old woman has malar rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, arthralgia and proteinuria. Which antibody correlates with disease activity and lupus nephritis?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Anti-dsDNA levels rise with activity, with low C3/C4; anti-Sm is highly specific but does not track activity.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 65-year-old man on procainamide develops arthralgia, serositis and positive ANA. Kidneys and CNS are spared. Which antibody is typically positive?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Drug-induced lupus (hydralazine, procainamide, isoniazid, minocycline, anti-TNF) has anti-histone antibodies and resolves on stopping the drug.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A patient with SLE has urine protein 2.5 g/day, active sediment and rising creatinine. Renal biopsy shows class IV diffuse proliferative nephritis. What is the recommended induction therapy?
o: Glucocorticoids plus mycophenolate mofetil (or IV cyclophosphamide), with hydroxychloroquine
msk-iii/medicine.e: Class III/IV lupus nephritis requires induction with MMF or low-dose cyclophosphamide plus steroids; belimumab or voclosporin may be added.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A patient on long-term hydroxychloroquine for SLE requires regular screening for which adverse effect?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Annual retinal screening (OCT and visual fields) after 5 years (earlier if risk factors); dose ≤5 mg/kg actual body weight.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 50-year-old man has sudden excruciating pain, redness and swelling of the first MTP joint after a wedding feast. What does joint aspiration show?
o: Needle-shaped, negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals
msk-iii/medicine.e: Gout: negatively birefringent needle-shaped urate crystals; pseudogout (CPPD): weakly positively birefringent rhomboid crystals.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A man has had four attacks of gout this year and tophi. When and how should allopurinol be started?
o: Start 900 mg/day during an acute attack without prophylaxis
Start low (100 mg/day) and titrate to serum urate <6 mg/dL, with colchicine or NSAID prophylaxis
Stop allopurinol whenever an acute flare occurs
Give allopurinol only during acute attacks
Never start allopurinol if tophi are present
msk-iii/medicine.e: Treat-to-target urate (<6 mg/dL; <5 with tophi). Flare prophylaxis for 3–6 months; do not stop allopurinol during flares. HLA-B*58:01 testing in high-risk ethnic groups.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 75-year-old woman develops an acute hot swollen knee after hip surgery. X-ray shows chondrocalcinosis. Which metabolic disorder should be screened for?
msk-iii/medicine.e: CPPD disease associations: hyperparathyroidism, haemochromatosis, hypomagnesaemia, hypophosphatasia.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 24-year-old man has low back pain and stiffness for 6 months that is worse in the morning, improves with exercise and wakes him at night. Which imaging finding is most sensitive for early disease?
o: Bone marrow oedema of the sacroiliac joints on MRI
msk-iii/medicine.e: Early axial spondyloarthritis may have normal X-rays; MRI STIR sequence shows sacroiliitis. Bamboo spine is a late radiographic sign.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A patient with ankylosing spondylitis has persistent high disease activity despite two NSAIDs at full dose for 4 weeks. What is the next step?
msk-iii/medicine.e: csDMARDs have no effect on axial disease; bDMARDs (TNFi, IL-17i) or JAK inhibitors are used after NSAID failure, with physiotherapy.

msk-iii/medicine.s: Three weeks after bloody diarrhoea, a 28-year-old man develops asymmetric knee arthritis, conjunctivitis and urethritis. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Reactive arthritis follows GI (Shigella, Salmonella, Campylobacter, Yersinia) or GU (Chlamydia) infection; associated with HLA-B27.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A patient with nail pitting and onycholysis has swelling of an entire finger ("sausage digit") and DIP joint involvement. X-ray shows "pencil-in-cup" deformity. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Psoriatic arthritis: dactylitis, DIP involvement, enthesitis, nail disease and pencil-in-cup deformity (arthritis mutilans).

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 70-year-old diabetic man has a hot, swollen knee with fever. Aspirate is turbid with WBC 80,000/mm³. What is the most common causative organism?
msk-iii/medicine.e: S. aureus is the most common cause of septic arthritis in adults; gonococcus in young sexually active adults. Needs IV antibiotics and joint washout.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 65-year-old obese woman has knee pain worse with activity and relieved by rest, brief morning stiffness under 30 minutes, and crepitus. X-ray shows joint space narrowing and osteophytes. What is the first-line management?
o: Weight loss, quadriceps strengthening exercise and education, with topical NSAIDs
msk-iii/medicine.e: NICE/OARSI: exercise, weight loss and education are core; topical NSAIDs before oral; arthroplasty when conservative care fails.

msk-iii/medicine.s: Bony swellings at the distal interphalangeal joints of the fingers in an elderly woman are called:
msk-iii/medicine.e: Heberden's nodes = DIP (OA); Bouchard's nodes = PIP (OA).

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 68-year-old postmenopausal woman has a DEXA scan of the hip. Which T-score defines osteoporosis?
msk-iii/medicine.e: WHO: normal ≥ −1.0; osteopenia −1.0 to −2.5; osteoporosis ≤ −2.5 (severe if with fragility fracture).

msk-iii/medicine.s: Which instruction is correct for a patient prescribed oral alendronate weekly?
o: Take with milk and calcium tablets at bedtime
Take on an empty stomach with a full glass of water and remain upright for 30 minutes
msk-iii/medicine.e: Alendronate can cause oesophagitis and absorption is poor with food/calcium; rare risks include osteonecrosis of the jaw and atypical femoral fractures.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 45-year-old woman has Raynaud's phenomenon, skin thickening proximal to the elbows and on the trunk, and dry cough. Which antibody is associated with this form and pulmonary fibrosis?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Diffuse cutaneous SSc: anti-Scl-70 (ILD risk) and anti-RNA polymerase III (renal crisis). Limited (CREST): anti-centromere (pulmonary hypertension).

msk-iii/medicine.s: A patient with diffuse systemic sclerosis develops accelerated hypertension and rising creatinine. What is the treatment of choice?
msk-iii/medicine.e: ACE inhibitors dramatically improved survival in scleroderma renal crisis; high-dose steroids (>15 mg/day prednisolone) can precipitate it.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 55-year-old man has proximal muscle weakness, a heliotrope rash on the eyelids and Gottron's papules. CK is raised. What is the most important associated condition to screen for?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Dermatomyositis in adults is associated with malignancy (lung, ovary, GI, nasopharyngeal); age-appropriate cancer screening is needed.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A patient with myositis has interstitial lung disease, mechanic's hands and Raynaud's. Which antibody is typically present?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Antisynthetase syndrome: anti-Jo-1, myositis, ILD, arthritis, Raynaud's and mechanic's hands.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 72-year-old woman has bilateral shoulder and pelvic girdle pain and stiffness for 6 weeks, with ESR 80 mm/h. CK is normal. What is the expected response to treatment?
o: No response to steroids, confirming diagnosis
Response to NSAIDs alone in all
Dramatic improvement within days on prednisolone 15 mg/day
msk-iii/medicine.e: PMR responds rapidly to low-dose steroids; lack of response should prompt reconsideration. Normal CK distinguishes from myositis.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 75-year-old man has new temporal headache, jaw claudication, scalp tenderness and transient blurred vision. ESR is 95 mm/h. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
o: Wait for biopsy result before any treatment
Prescribe NSAIDs and review in 1 week
Start high-dose prednisolone immediately, then arrange temporal artery ultrasound/biopsy
msk-iii/medicine.e: Visual symptoms threaten permanent blindness; steroids should not be delayed for biopsy (biopsy remains positive for 1–2 weeks).

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 50-year-old woman has dry eyes, dry mouth and bilateral parotid swelling. Schirmer test is positive. Which antibodies are typically positive?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Sjögren syndrome has a 15–20 fold increased risk of B-cell (MALT) lymphoma; anti-Ro in pregnancy risks congenital heart block.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 45-year-old man has chronic sinusitis with bloody nasal discharge, haemoptysis with cavitating lung nodules and haematuria with red cell casts. Which antibody is expected?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis: upper and lower respiratory tract + glomerulonephritis; c-ANCA/PR3. EGPA has asthma, eosinophilia and p-ANCA.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 40-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B develops hypertension, mononeuritis multiplex, livedo reticularis and testicular pain. Angiography shows microaneurysms of renal and mesenteric arteries. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/medicine.e: PAN is a medium-vessel vasculitis, ANCA-negative, associated with hepatitis B, sparing the lungs and glomeruli.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old man has recurrent oral and genital ulcers, uveitis and a positive pathergy test. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Behçet: recurrent oral aphthae plus genital ulcers, eye lesions, skin lesions and pathergy; common along the Silk Road; HLA-B51.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 25-year-old woman has arm claudication, absent radial pulse on the left, BP difference of 30 mmHg between arms and a subclavian bruit. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Takayasu ("pulseless disease") is a large-vessel granulomatous vasculitis of the aorta and branches in young women, especially Asian.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 28-year-old has daily spiking evening fevers, salmon-pink evanescent rash, arthralgia, sore throat, and ferritin 9,000 ng/mL. ANA and RF are negative. What is the likely diagnosis?
msk-iii/medicine.e: AOSD is a diagnosis of exclusion (infection, malignancy); markedly raised ferritin with low glycosylated ferritin is characteristic.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A patient has overlapping features of SLE, systemic sclerosis and polymyositis, with Raynaud's and puffy hands. Which antibody is characteristic?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Mixed connective tissue disease is defined by high-titre anti-U1 RNP antibodies; pulmonary hypertension is a major cause of death.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 38-year-old woman has chronic widespread pain for over 3 months, fatigue, unrefreshing sleep and multiple tender points. All blood tests are normal. What is the best initial management?
o: Patient education and graded aerobic exercise, with amitriptyline or duloxetine if needed
msk-iii/medicine.e: EULAR: non-pharmacological therapy (exercise) first; low-dose amitriptyline, duloxetine or pregabalin for pain/sleep.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 70-year-old man has bone pain, enlarging skull, and isolated raised alkaline phosphatase with normal calcium and phosphate. X-ray shows thickened cortex and mixed lytic-sclerotic lesions. What is the treatment for symptomatic disease?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Paget's disease (increased disorganized bone remodelling) responds to bisphosphonates, zoledronate being most effective; complications include deafness and osteosarcoma.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 35-year-old woman who wears full veil and stays indoors has proximal myopathy, bone pain and waddling gait. Labs show low calcium, low phosphate, high ALP and high PTH. What is the diagnosis?
o: Osteomalacia due to vitamin D deficiency
msk-iii/medicine.e: Vitamin D deficiency is common in Pakistan; osteomalacia causes Looser's zones (pseudofractures). Osteoporosis has normal biochemistry.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A patient started on atorvastatin and clarithromycin develops severe muscle pain, dark urine and CK of 25,000 U/L. What is the most likely diagnosis?
o: Statin-induced rhabdomyolysis due to drug interaction (CYP3A4 inhibition)
msk-iii/medicine.e: Macrolides inhibit CYP3A4, raising statin levels; stop both, give aggressive IV fluids to prevent AKI.

msk-iii/medicine.s: Which feature in a patient with low back pain requires urgent MRI and surgical referral?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Cauda equina syndrome (saddle anaesthesia, bladder/bowel dysfunction, bilateral sciatica) is a surgical emergency.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A shepherd from a rural area has undulant fever, sweating, arthralgia and sacroiliitis. He drinks unpasteurized milk. What is the recommended treatment?
o: Doxycycline for 6 weeks plus streptomycin (or gentamicin) or rifampicin
msk-iii/medicine.e: Brucellosis needs combination therapy (doxycycline + aminoglycoside or rifampicin) for at least 6 weeks; longer for spondylitis.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A tall 20-year-old man has arachnodactyly, joint hypermobility, lens dislocation upwards and a high-arched palate. Which cardiovascular complication is most important to monitor?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Marfan syndrome (FBN1, autosomal dominant) – annual echocardiography for aortic root; beta-blockers/ARBs slow dilatation.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 50-year-old woman has sudden severe shoulder pain with painful arc between 60° and 120° of abduction. X-ray shows calcification in the supraspinatus tendon. What is the diagnosis?
o: Calcific tendinitis of the rotator cuff (supraspinatus)
msk-iii/medicine.e: Painful arc 60–120° indicates supraspinatus impingement/tendinopathy; frozen shoulder causes global loss of active and passive movement, especially external rotation.

msk-iii/medicine.s: A 55-year-old diabetic woman has progressive shoulder pain with marked restriction of both active and passive external rotation. X-ray is normal. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/medicine.e: Frozen shoulder is associated with diabetes; loss of passive external rotation is characteristic; it is usually self-limiting over 1–3 years.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A 6-year-old boy falls on an outstretched hand and has a displaced extension-type supracondylar fracture of the humerus. His radial pulse is absent and hand is pale. Which structure is at greatest risk?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Brachial artery injury (and anterior interosseous branch of median nerve) is common; pulseless pale hand needs urgent closed reduction and pinning. Watch for Volkmann's ischaemic contracture.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A 65-year-old woman falls on an outstretched hand. X-ray shows a distal radius fracture with dorsal displacement and angulation of the distal fragment ("dinner fork" deformity). What is the fracture?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Colles: dorsal displacement; Smith: volar displacement (reverse Colles); Barton: intra-articular with carpal subluxation.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A 22-year-old has tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox after a fall. Initial wrist X-rays are normal. What is the next best step?
o: Immobilize in a splint/cast and arrange MRI (or repeat X-ray at 10–14 days)
Reassure and discharge with no immobilization
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Scaphoid fractures may not show early; blood supply enters distally, so the proximal pole risks avascular necrosis and non-union.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: An 80-year-old woman falls and has a shortened, externally rotated leg. X-ray shows a displaced intracapsular (Garden IV) fracture of the femoral neck. What is the treatment of choice?
o: Hemiarthroplasty (or total hip replacement if active and fit)
Bed rest with traction for 12 weeks
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Displaced intracapsular fractures disrupt retinacular vessels (AVN risk), so replacement is preferred in the elderly; extracapsular fractures are fixed with DHS/IM nail.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: Six hours after a plaster cast for tibial shaft fracture, the patient has severe pain unrelieved by opioids and pain on passive stretching of toes. Dorsalis pedis pulse is palpable. What is the immediate management?
o: Remove/split the cast down to skin and proceed to urgent fasciotomy if symptoms persist
Wait for loss of pulse to confirm
Order Doppler ultrasound and review in 24 hours
Elevate the limb above heart level and give more morphine
Apply ice packs and tighten the cast
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Pain out of proportion and on passive stretch is the earliest sign; pulses are usually present. Limb should be kept at heart level (not elevated). Fasciotomy for compartment pressure within 30 mmHg of diastolic.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A motorcyclist has a tibial fracture with a 12 cm wound, extensive soft tissue damage and periosteal stripping requiring flap coverage. What is the Gustilo–Anderson grade?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: IIIA: adequate soft tissue coverage; IIIB: periosteal stripping requiring flap; IIIC: arterial injury needing repair. Give IV antibiotics within 1 hour, debridement and stabilization.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: Two days after bilateral femoral shaft fractures, a 25-year-old man becomes confused, hypoxic and has petechiae over the axilla and conjunctiva. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: FES (Gurd's criteria): respiratory insufficiency, cerebral involvement and petechial rash 24–72 h after long bone fracture; early fixation reduces risk.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: After an anterior shoulder dislocation, a patient has loss of sensation over the "regimental badge" area of the upper arm. Which nerve is injured?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Axillary nerve (C5, C6) supplies deltoid and skin over its lower half; test before and after reduction.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A fracture of the mid-shaft of the humerus causes wrist drop. Which nerve is injured?
o: Radial nerve in the spiral groove
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Radial nerve palsy is usually neurapraxia and recovers; manage expectantly with wrist splint and monitor.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A child falls and sustains a fracture of the proximal third of the ulna. What associated injury must be looked for?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Monteggia: proximal ulna fracture + radial head dislocation. Galeazzi: distal radius fracture + DRUJ dislocation.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A newborn girl born by breech delivery has a "clunk" when the flexed hip is abducted and lifted forward. What is the recommended treatment?
o: Hip spica after open reduction immediately
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Positive Ortolani (reducing a dislocated hip); Barlow dislocates a reducible hip. Pavlik harness under 6 months; ultrasound is the imaging of choice before 4–6 months.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A newborn has a rigid foot deformity with cavus, adductus, varus and equinus. What is the preferred treatment?
o: Ponseti method of serial casting with percutaneous Achilles tenotomy and foot abduction brace
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Ponseti method has >90% success; correction order is CAVE (cavus, adductus, varus, equinus). Bracing prevents relapse.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A 6-year-old boy has a limp and knee pain for 2 months. Hip abduction and internal rotation are restricted. X-ray shows flattening and sclerosis of the femoral head. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Perthes is idiopathic avascular necrosis of the femoral head, age 4–8, boys; hip pathology often presents as knee pain.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: An obese 13-year-old boy has a limp and knee pain. On flexing the hip, it rolls into external rotation. Frog-leg lateral X-ray shows posterior-inferior displacement of the femoral epiphysis. What is the treatment?
o: In situ fixation with a single cannulated screw, non-weight bearing
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: SCFE is managed with pinning in situ; forceful reduction risks AVN. Consider prophylactic fixation of the other side in high-risk patients.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: An 8-year-old has fever and severe pain at the lower femoral metaphysis with refusal to bear weight. X-ray is normal. What is the most sensitive early imaging?
o: Plain X-ray repeated the same day
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: X-ray changes take 10–14 days; MRI shows early marrow oedema and subperiosteal abscess. S. aureus is the commonest organism.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A 15-year-old has pain and swelling around the knee. X-ray shows a destructive metaphyseal lesion of the distal femur with Codman's triangle and "sunburst" periosteal reaction. What is the likely diagnosis?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Osteosarcoma: metaphysis of long bones around the knee in adolescents; lungs are the commonest metastatic site. Treatment: neoadjuvant chemotherapy, limb salvage surgery.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A 12-year-old has fever, raised ESR and a diaphyseal femoral lesion with "onion-skin" periosteal reaction. Which translocation is characteristic?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Ewing sarcoma: small round blue cells, CD99 positive, t(11;22); may mimic osteomyelitis; chemo- and radio-sensitive.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A 30-year-old woman has an eccentric, lytic, "soap-bubble" lesion extending to the subchondral bone of the distal radius. What is the likely diagnosis?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: GCT occurs at epiphyses after physeal closure (20–40 years); locally aggressive; treated with extended curettage; denosumab for difficult cases.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A 30-year-old man from rural KP has back pain, evening fever, weight loss and a gibbus at T10. MRI shows destruction of two adjacent vertebral bodies with disc involvement and paravertebral abscess. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: TB spine typically involves adjacent vertebrae and the disc (paradiscal); metastases usually spare the disc. Treat with ATT (≥9–12 months); surgery for neurological deficit or instability.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A 35-year-old man has back pain radiating down the lateral leg to the dorsum of the foot, weak great toe extension and a positive straight leg raise. Which nerve root is affected?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: L5: weak EHL/ankle dorsiflexion, sensory loss on dorsum; L4: knee reflex, medial leg; S1: ankle reflex, plantar flexion, lateral foot.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A 45-year-old pregnant woman has nocturnal tingling of the thumb, index and middle fingers. Which test reproduces symptoms by holding the wrists fully flexed for 60 seconds?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Phalen's and Tinel's (over the carpal tunnel) support median nerve compression; nerve conduction studies confirm. Finkelstein's test is for De Quervain's tenosynovitis.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A footballer twists his knee, hears a "pop" and develops a haemarthrosis within 2 hours. Which clinical test is most sensitive for the likely injury?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Rapid haemarthrosis suggests ACL rupture; Lachman test is most sensitive; McMurray tests meniscal tears.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A child has multiple fractures with minimal trauma, blue sclerae and hearing loss. What is the underlying defect?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Osteogenesis imperfecta is mostly autosomal dominant type I collagen defect; bisphosphonates reduce fracture rate.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A 35-year-old man on long-term high-dose steroids for nephrotic syndrome has groin pain with normal X-ray. What is the most sensitive investigation for early avascular necrosis of the femoral head?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: MRI detects early AVN (double-line sign) before X-ray changes; risk factors: steroids, alcohol, sickle cell, trauma.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A 16-year-old has a painless hard swelling near the knee. X-ray shows a bony projection pointing away from the joint with a cartilage cap, continuous with the medullary cavity. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Osteochondroma is the commonest benign bone tumour; malignant change is suggested by pain, growth after skeletal maturity, or cartilage cap >2 cm.

msk-iii/orthopaedics.s: A 17-year-old boy has night pain in the tibia dramatically relieved by aspirin. CT shows a small radiolucent nidus with surrounding sclerosis. What is the preferred treatment?
msk-iii/orthopaedics.e: Osteoid osteoma (nidus <1.5 cm) pain is prostaglandin-mediated and relieved by NSAIDs; RFA is the treatment of choice.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: A 4-year-old has quotidian spiking fevers for 3 weeks, evanescent salmon-coloured rash, arthritis, hepatosplenomegaly and very high ferritin. Which life-threatening complication should be watched for?
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: Systemic JIA can develop MAS (secondary HLH) with falling ESR, cytopenias, falling fibrinogen and very high ferritin; IL-1/IL-6 blockade is used.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: A 3-year-old girl has a swollen, painless left knee for 8 weeks. ANA is positive. Which screening is most important?
o: Regular slit-lamp examination for anterior uveitis
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: ANA-positive oligoarticular JIA in young girls has the highest risk of asymptomatic chronic anterior uveitis, which can cause blindness.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: An 18-month-old child has bowed legs, widened wrists, rachitic rosary and delayed walking. Labs: low calcium, low phosphate, high ALP, low 25-OH vitamin D. What is the appropriate treatment?
o: Vitamin D (cholecalciferol) replacement with calcium supplementation
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: Nutritional rickets: vitamin D (e.g., 2000 IU daily for 12 weeks, or stoss therapy) plus calcium; X-ray shows cupping and fraying of metaphyses.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: A child has rickets with normal calcium, very low phosphate, high urinary phosphate wasting and normal 25-OH vitamin D. The father has short stature and bowed legs. What is the diagnosis?
o: X-linked hypophosphataemic rickets (PHEX mutation, FGF23 excess)
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: XLH (X-linked dominant) does not respond to vitamin D; treated with oral phosphate + calcitriol or burosumab (anti-FGF23).

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: A 6-year-old boy has palpable purpura on the buttocks and legs, abdominal pain, and swollen ankles following a sore throat. Platelet count is normal. What is the most important long-term monitoring?
o: Urinalysis and blood pressure for renal involvement
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: IgA vasculitis: renal involvement determines prognosis; monitor urine and BP for 6–12 months. Watch for intussusception.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: A 5-year-old has a limp for 1 day after a cold. Which finding favours septic arthritis rather than transient synovitis of the hip (Kocher criteria)?
o: Afebrile, able to bear weight, normal ESR
Fever >38.5°C, non-weight bearing, ESR >40 mm/h and WBC >12 × 10⁹/L
Mild limp with full range of movement
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: Kocher criteria: fever, non-weight bearing, ESR >40, WBC >12,000 (CRP >20 added). Probability rises with number of criteria; aspirate under ultrasound.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: A 7-year-old girl has difficulty climbing stairs, violaceous eyelid rash and scaly papules over the knuckles. CK is raised. Which late complication is more common in the juvenile form than in adults?
o: Calcinosis of skin and soft tissue
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: JDM is not associated with malignancy but frequently causes calcinosis and vasculopathy; treat with steroids and methotrexate.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: A 14-month-old child fed boiled cow's milk only has irritability, refuses to walk, lies in "frog-leg" position and has swollen bleeding gums around erupted teeth. What is the likely deficiency?
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: Scurvy causes subperiosteal haemorrhages (pseudoparalysis), scorbutic rosary and perifollicular haemorrhages; X-ray shows Wimberger's ring and Frankel's line.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: A child has short limbs (rhizomelia), large head with frontal bossing, trident hands and normal intelligence. What is the genetic defect?
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: Achondroplasia is autosomal dominant (80% de novo, advanced paternal age); risk of foramen magnum stenosis. Vosoritide is a newer therapy.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: A 3-month-old infant has profound hypotonia ("floppy"), tongue fasciculations, absent reflexes, but is alert with good eye contact. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: SMA (SMN1 deletion) affects anterior horn cells; tongue fasciculations and areflexia with preserved cognition. Nusinersen, risdiplam and gene therapy are available.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: Which is the most common cause of death in Duchenne muscular dystrophy?
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: Progressive respiratory muscle weakness and dilated cardiomyopathy; steroids (prednisolone/deflazacort) prolong ambulation; non-invasive ventilation improves survival.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: A 6-year-old has bilateral leg pains in the evenings, relieved by massage, with no limp, normal activity and normal examination. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Reassurance, massage and simple analgesia with no investigations
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: Benign nocturnal limb pains are bilateral, not in joints, and never cause limp; red flags (unilateral, joint swelling, fever, weight loss, night waking) need workup.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: A 2-year-old has coarse facial features, corneal clouding, hepatosplenomegaly, gibbus, and developmental regression. Urine shows raised dermatan and heparan sulphate. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: Hurler (alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency) has corneal clouding; Hunter (X-linked) has no corneal clouding. Treatment: enzyme replacement/HSCT.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: A 3-year-old obese child who walked early has progressive unilateral bowing of the tibia. X-ray shows a beak-like medial proximal tibial metaphysis. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: Physiological bowing resolves by 2 years; progressive/asymmetric bowing after 2 years suggests Blount disease; metaphyseal–diaphyseal angle >11°.

msk-iii/paediatrics.s: A 13-year-old girl has fever, malar rash, arthritis, haemolytic anaemia and nephritis. Compared with adult-onset SLE, childhood-onset SLE is characterised by:
o: Milder disease with no renal involvement
