More frequent and severe renal and haematological involvement
msk-iii/paediatrics.e: Childhood SLE is more severe with higher rates of nephritis, cytopenias and neuropsychiatric involvement.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 30-year-old man has well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scales on the elbows, knees and scalp. Removing the scale produces pinpoint bleeding. What is this sign called?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Auspitz sign (punctate bleeding on scale removal) is characteristic of psoriasis; Koebner phenomenon is lesions at sites of trauma.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A patient with stable psoriasis develops a severe flare after starting a new drug for bipolar disorder. Which drug is the likely trigger?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Lithium, beta-blockers, antimalarials, NSAIDs and withdrawal of systemic steroids can exacerbate psoriasis.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A patient with extensive plaque psoriasis (PASI 18) and psoriatic arthritis has failed topical therapy. Which systemic drug treats both skin and joints and is first-line?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Methotrexate is effective for skin and peripheral joints. Systemic steroids cause rebound/pustular psoriasis; biologics for failure of conventional therapy.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 40-year-old woman has pruritic, purple, polygonal, flat-topped papules on the flexor wrists with fine white lines on the surface, and lacy white patches on buccal mucosa. Which infection should be screened for?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: The 6 Ps of lichen planus with Wickham's striae; association with hepatitis C. Histology: saw-tooth rete ridges, band-like lymphocytic infiltrate.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 45-year-old has painful oral erosions for 2 months followed by flaccid bullae on the trunk that rupture easily. Nikolsky sign is positive. What does direct immunofluorescence show?
o: Linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane
Intercellular IgG deposition in a "fishnet" pattern in the epidermis
Granular IgA in the dermal papillae
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Pemphigus vulgaris: anti-desmoglein 3 (±1); intraepidermal suprabasal split with acantholysis ("tombstone" basal cells).

msk-iii/dermatology.s: An 80-year-old man has intensely itchy, tense bullae on the flexures of limbs and trunk on an urticarial base. Mucosa is spared. Nikolsky sign is negative. What is the target antigen?
o: BP180 (collagen XVII) and BP230 in hemidesmosomes
msk-iii/dermatology.e: BP: subepidermal blister, linear IgG/C3 at BMZ; associated with DPP-4 inhibitors (gliptins). Treated with potent topical steroids (clobetasol).

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 25-year-old has intensely itchy grouped vesicles on the elbows, knees and buttocks. Direct immunofluorescence shows granular IgA in the dermal papillae. What is the associated condition and treatment?
o: Coeliac disease; gluten-free diet and dapsone
msk-iii/dermatology.e: DH is the cutaneous manifestation of gluten-sensitive enteropathy; check G6PD before dapsone.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: Ten days after starting carbamazepine, a 30-year-old develops fever, painful dusky targetoid lesions, mucosal erosions of the lips, eyes and genitals, and 40% epidermal detachment. What is the diagnosis and key first step?
o: Toxic epidermal necrolysis; stop the drug immediately and admit to burns/ICU
msk-iii/dermatology.e: SJS <10%, overlap 10–30%, TEN >30% BSA detachment. Culprits: carbamazepine (HLA-B*15:02), allopurinol, lamotrigine, sulfonamides, nevirapine. SCORTEN predicts mortality.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: Three weeks after starting allopurinol, a patient develops fever, facial oedema, widespread morbilliform rash, lymphadenopathy, eosinophilia and raised liver enzymes. What is the diagnosis?
o: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
msk-iii/dermatology.e: DRESS has a long latency (2–8 weeks), eosinophilia and internal organ involvement; stop drug and give systemic steroids.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 2-year-old child has itchy, dry, lichenified eczema in the antecubital and popliteal fossae, with family history of asthma. What is the mainstay of treatment?
o: Regular emollients with topical corticosteroids for flares
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Emollients restore the barrier; topical steroids or calcineurin inhibitors for flares; filaggrin mutations predispose.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A woman develops an itchy eczematous rash on the earlobes and under a metal watch buckle. Which test confirms the allergen?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Allergic contact dermatitis (type IV hypersensitivity, commonly nickel) is confirmed by patch testing; prick tests are for type I allergies.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 17-year-old girl has severe nodulocystic acne with scarring despite 3 months of oral doxycycline and topical therapy. What is the treatment of choice and the essential precaution?
o: Oral isotretinoin with pregnancy prevention programme
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Isotretinoin is highly teratogenic; requires contraception, pregnancy tests, lipid/LFT monitoring and mood monitoring.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 45-year-old woman has facial flushing, persistent central facial erythema, telangiectasia and papulopustules without comedones. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Absence of comedones distinguishes rosacea from acne; triggers include heat, alcohol, spicy food; avoid topical steroids. Treat with topical ivermectin/metronidazole, oral doxycycline.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 20-year-old has depigmented, chalk-white, well-defined macules on the hands and around the mouth that accentuate under Wood's lamp. Which associated condition should be screened for?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Vitiligo is associated with thyroid disease, pernicious anaemia, diabetes and Addison's; treatments include topical steroids/calcineurin inhibitors, NB-UVB and ruxolitinib cream.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 30-year-old woman on oral contraceptives has symmetrical brown macules on the cheeks and forehead that worsen in summer. What is the most important component of management?
o: Strict broad-spectrum sun protection with topical hydroquinone/triple combination cream
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Melasma is driven by UV/visible light and hormones; photoprotection (including visible light with tinted sunscreens) is essential; tranexamic acid is an adjunct.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A family presents with severe nocturnal itching. Examination shows burrows in finger web spaces, wrists and genital papules. What is the treatment?
o: Permethrin 5% cream to the whole body from neck down, repeated after 7 days, treating all household contacts simultaneously
msk-iii/dermatology.e: All close contacts must be treated simultaneously; wash bedding/clothes at 60°C. Oral ivermectin for crusted scabies or outbreaks.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 7-year-old boy has a scaly patch of hair loss with broken hairs and a boggy, pustular swelling (kerion) on the scalp. What is the correct treatment?
o: Oral antifungal (griseofulvin or terbinafine) for several weeks
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Tinea capitis requires systemic antifungals since topicals don't penetrate hair follicles; kerion is inflammatory, not a bacterial abscess.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A young man has hypopigmented, finely scaling macules on the upper trunk that become more visible after sun exposure. KOH shows "spaghetti and meatballs". What is the causative organism?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Pityriasis versicolor (Malassezia) is treated with topical ketoconazole/selenium sulfide; recurrence is common.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A man from Khyber district has a painless, crusted ulcer with raised indurated border on his cheek that started as a papule 3 months ago. Slit-skin smear shows amastigotes (LD bodies). What is a first-line treatment for a single lesion?
o: Excision with skin grafting as first line
Intralesional sodium stibogluconate (meglumine antimoniate) or cryotherapy
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Cutaneous leishmaniasis ("oriental sore", L. tropica/major) is endemic in KP and Balochistan; intralesional antimonials are used for limited lesions, systemic for multiple/complex ones.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A patient has 3 hypopigmented, anaesthetic patches with a thickened ulnar nerve. Slit-skin smear is negative. According to WHO, how is this classified and treated?
o: Paucibacillary leprosy; rifampicin, dapsone and clofazimine for 6 months
Multibacillary leprosy; 12 months of rifampicin alone
msk-iii/dermatology.e: WHO: PB = 1–5 lesions, smear negative; MB = >5 lesions or smear positive. WHO now recommends the 3-drug regimen for both (6 months PB, 12 months MB).

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A patient with lepromatous leprosy on treatment develops fever, crops of tender red nodules on the limbs, neuritis and arthralgia. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: ENL is immune-complex mediated in MB leprosy; treated with steroids, thalidomide, or clofazimine. Type 1 reaction is cell-mediated inflammation of existing lesions.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A young woman has a slowly enlarging reddish-brown plaque on the cheek. Diascopy shows "apple-jelly" nodules. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Lupus vulgaris is paucibacillary cutaneous TB in a previously sensitized host; treat with standard ATT.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 70-year-old man has painful grouped vesicles in a band on the right chest wall, not crossing the midline, for 2 days. What is the most appropriate treatment?
o: Oral valaciclovir (or aciclovir) within 72 hours plus analgesia
Wait and watch with no antivirals
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Antivirals reduce acute pain and duration; post-herpetic neuralgia is common in elderly (treat with amitriptyline/gabapentin/pregabalin). Hutchinson's sign (nasal tip) predicts ocular involvement.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 5-year-old has honey-coloured crusts around the nose and mouth. What is the most common causative organism?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Non-bullous impetigo: S. aureus (and S. pyogenes); localised: topical fusidic acid/mupirocin; extensive: oral flucloxacillin. Post-streptococcal GN may follow.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 50-year-old has a pigmented lesion on the back that is asymmetrical, has irregular borders, varied colour and is 9 mm in diameter, recently enlarging. What is the most important prognostic factor after excision?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Breslow thickness (mm) is the single most important prognostic factor; do an excision biopsy with 2 mm margin, then wide local excision.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 70-year-old farmer has a slow-growing pearly nodule with rolled edges and telangiectasia near the inner canthus, now with central ulceration. What is the treatment of choice for this site?
o: Radiotherapy only as first choice for all
msk-iii/dermatology.e: BCC (rodent ulcer) rarely metastasises but is locally destructive; Mohs surgery gives highest cure with tissue sparing for high-risk facial sites.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 60-year-old has a rapidly growing ulcer on the edge of an old burn scar on the leg. What is this lesion called?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Marjolin's ulcer is SCC arising in chronic scars; it is aggressive and requires wide excision; lymph nodes should be assessed.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 35-year-old has had itchy transient wheals lasting under 24 hours, occurring almost daily for 4 months, without angioedema or triggers. What is first-line treatment?
o: Second-generation H1 antihistamine, up-dosed up to four times the standard dose if needed
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (>6 weeks): non-sedating antihistamines; omalizumab then ciclosporin for refractory disease.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 22-year-old has well-defined round patches of complete hair loss on the scalp with "exclamation mark" hairs at the margins. Skin is normal. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/dermatology.e: Autoimmune non-scarring alopecia; treat with intralesional steroids; JAK inhibitors (baricitinib, ritlecitinib) for extensive disease.

msk-iii/dermatology.s: A 25-year-old woman has painful red nodules on both shins with fever and arthralgia. Which investigation is most relevant in Pakistan to find the cause?
o: Chest X-ray and tuberculin/IGRA test (with ASO titre)
msk-iii/dermatology.e: EN is a septal panniculitis; causes include streptococcal infection, TB, sarcoidosis (bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy), IBD, drugs (OCP) and pregnancy.

msk-iii/plastic-surgery.s: Which statement about split-thickness skin grafts compared with full-thickness grafts is correct?
o: They take more readily but show more secondary contraction
The donor site requires primary closure
They have less contraction and better colour match
msk-iii/plastic-surgery.e: STSG: epidermis + part of dermis, good take, heals donor site spontaneously, more secondary contraction; FTSG: better cosmesis (face), more primary contraction, donor site closed primarily.

msk-iii/plastic-surgery.s: What is the most common cause of skin graft failure?
o: Haematoma or seroma beneath the graft
msk-iii/plastic-surgery.e: Fluid collection prevents plasmatic imbibition and inosculation; other causes include shearing movement and infection (β-haemolytic Streptococcus).

msk-iii/plastic-surgery.s: According to common protocols, when is primary cleft lip repair usually performed?
msk-iii/plastic-surgery.e: Rule of 10s (10 weeks, 10 lb, Hb 10 g/dL) for lip repair; palate repair at 6–12 months before speech develops.

msk-iii/plastic-surgery.s: A 25-year-old develops a raised scar that extends beyond the boundaries of the original ear-piercing wound and continues to grow after 1 year. What is the diagnosis and first-line treatment?
msk-iii/plastic-surgery.e: Keloids extend beyond wound margins and rarely regress; excision alone has high recurrence, so combine with steroid or radiotherapy. Hypertrophic scars stay within wound margins.

msk-iii/plastic-surgery.s: A bedridden stroke patient has a sacral ulcer with full-thickness skin loss and exposed subcutaneous fat but no bone, tendon or muscle visible. What is the stage?
msk-iii/plastic-surgery.e: NPIAP: stage 1 non-blanchable erythema; 2 partial thickness; 3 full-thickness to fat; 4 exposed bone/tendon/muscle; unstageable if base obscured by slough/eschar.

msk-iii/plastic-surgery.s: A 25-year-old cuts the palm of his hand with glass between the distal palmar crease and the middle of the middle phalanx. He cannot flex the DIP or PIP joints. Which zone of flexor tendon injury is this, historically called "no man's land"?
msk-iii/plastic-surgery.e: Zone II contains both FDS and FDP within the fibro-osseous sheath; primary repair by an expert with early protected mobilization gives the best results.

msk-iii/plastic-surgery.s: A lineman sustains a high-voltage electrical injury with small entry and exit wounds. Which complication is most important to anticipate early?
o: Cardiac arrhythmia, deep muscle necrosis with rhabdomyolysis and compartment syndrome
msk-iii/plastic-surgery.e: Visible wounds underestimate deep tissue damage; ECG monitoring, aggressive fluids for myoglobinuria (urine output 1–1.5 mL/kg/h) and early fasciotomy.

msk-iii/plastic-surgery.s: Which technique is used to lengthen a linear scar contracture across a flexion crease?
msk-iii/plastic-surgery.e: Z-plasty transposes two triangular flaps (60° angles gain ~75% length) to lengthen and reorient scars.

msk-iii/psychiatry.s: A 24-year-old woman repeatedly visits aesthetic clinics requesting procedures for a "deformed" nose. Examination is normal. She spends hours checking mirrors and avoids social contact. What is the best management?
o: Refer for psychiatric evaluation; CBT with SSRI rather than cosmetic procedures
msk-iii/psychiatry.e: Cosmetic procedures rarely help BDD and may worsen distress; SSRIs (often high dose) and CBT are effective.

msk-iii/psychiatry.s: A 12-year-old girl has irregular patches of hair loss with hairs broken at different lengths. Hair pull test is negative and skin is normal. She admits relief when pulling hair. What is the diagnosis?
msk-iii/psychiatry.e: Trichotillomania is an obsessive-compulsive related disorder; habit reversal therapy is first-line. Watch for trichobezoar with hair eating.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 58-year-old man has crushing chest pain. ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF with ST depression in I and aVL. Which coronary artery is most likely occluded?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Inferior STEMI is usually due to RCA occlusion (≈80%); check right-sided leads (V4R) for RV infarction.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with inferior STEMI becomes hypotensive after sublingual glyceryl trinitrate. JVP is raised and lungs are clear. ST elevation is present in V4R. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
o: IV fluid bolus and avoid nitrates/diuretics while arranging reperfusion
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: RV infarction is preload dependent; nitrates, diuretics and opioids can cause profound hypotension.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 55-year-old man presents 2 hours after onset of anterior STEMI to a hospital without a cath lab. The nearest PCI centre is 3 hours away. What is the best reperfusion strategy?
o: Fibrinolysis (e.g., tenecteplase/streptokinase) within 10 minutes of diagnosis, then transfer for angiography
Transfer for primary PCI regardless of delay
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Primary PCI is preferred if achievable within 120 minutes of diagnosis; otherwise fibrinolysis within 12 h of symptom onset, followed by a pharmaco-invasive strategy.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which of the following is an ABSOLUTE contraindication to thrombolysis in STEMI?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Absolute: any prior intracranial haemorrhage, ischaemic stroke within 3–6 months, CNS neoplasm, active bleeding, aortic dissection, major head trauma within 3 weeks.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Five days after an anterior MI, a patient develops sudden breathlessness, hypotension and a new loud pansystolic murmur at the left sternal edge with a thrill. Oxygen saturation step-up is found between the right atrium and right ventricle. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: VSR: new harsh pansystolic murmur with thrill and O₂ step-up; papillary muscle rupture causes acute MR with pulmonary oedema, murmur at apex.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Three weeks after MI, a patient has pleuritic chest pain, fever, pericardial rub and raised ESR. What is the treatment?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Dressler (post-MI) syndrome is an autoimmune pericarditis; treat like pericarditis with aspirin and colchicine.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Six weeks after an anterior MI, an ECG shows persistent ST elevation in V1–V4 without chest pain. Echocardiography shows a dyskinetic apical segment. What is the likely diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Persistent ST elevation after MI suggests LV aneurysm; risks include heart failure, arrhythmias and mural thrombus (anticoagulate if thrombus).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 65-year-old diabetic woman has ongoing chest pain with ST depression in V4–V6 and raised high-sensitivity troponin. BP is stable. In addition to aspirin, which antithrombotic combination is appropriate?
o: A P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor or clopidogrel) plus fondaparinux or enoxaparin
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Fibrinolysis has no role in NSTE-ACS; DAPT plus parenteral anticoagulant with early invasive strategy guided by risk (GRACE score).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which combination is recommended for long-term secondary prevention after an MI with LVEF 35%?
o: Aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitor for 12 months, high-intensity statin, beta-blocker, ACE inhibitor/ARNI, mineralocorticoid antagonist, SGLT2 inhibitor
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Post-MI with LV systolic dysfunction requires full prognostic therapy plus cardiac rehabilitation and smoking cessation.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 60-year-old man has exertional chest tightness relieved by rest within 5 minutes. Resting ECG is normal. What is the recommended first-line investigation according to NICE/ESC?
o: CT coronary angiography (or functional non-invasive testing)
Invasive coronary angiography in all cases
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: For suspected stable CAD, CTCA (or stress imaging depending on pre-test probability) is first-line.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 35-year-old woman has chest pain at rest early in the morning with transient ST elevation that resolves spontaneously. Angiography shows normal coronaries. What is the drug of choice?
o: Calcium channel blocker (e.g., diltiazem or amlodipine)
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Prinzmetal angina is due to coronary vasospasm; beta-blockers can worsen spasm; avoid triggers (smoking, cocaine, triptans).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 62-year-old man has heart failure with LVEF 30%. He is on ramipril and furosemide. Which drugs have been shown to reduce mortality and should be added?
o: Ivabradine as first-line instead of beta-blocker
Beta-blocker (bisoprolol/carvedilol), mineralocorticoid antagonist and SGLT2 inhibitor; consider switching ACEi to sacubitril–valsartan
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: The four pillars of HFrEF: ARNI/ACEi/ARB, evidence-based beta-blocker, MRA and SGLT2i. Diuretics relieve congestion but don't reduce mortality.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient on enalapril is to be switched to sacubitril–valsartan. What is the required interval?
o: Stop enalapril at least 36 hours before starting sacubitril–valsartan
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Combined neprilysin and ACE inhibition greatly increases angioedema risk; a 36-hour washout is required.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 70-year-old woman presents with severe breathlessness, frothy pink sputum, BP 170/100 mmHg and SpO₂ 84% on air with bilateral crackles. What is the most appropriate initial management?
o: Lie flat and give IV fluids
Sit upright, oxygen/CPAP, IV furosemide and IV nitrate infusion
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Hypertensive acute HF: vasodilators (nitrates) and diuretics with non-invasive ventilation if hypoxic; routine morphine is no longer recommended.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A breathless 72-year-old has an NT-proBNP of 80 pg/mL. What is the significance of this result?
o: It makes heart failure very unlikely (high negative predictive value)
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Low natriuretic peptides effectively exclude HF (NT-proBNP <125 pg/mL chronic, <300 acute); raised levels need echocardiography.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: An elderly woman on digoxin and furosemide has nausea, yellow-green vision and a bradyarrhythmia. Which electrolyte abnormality most increases the risk of this toxicity?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Hypokalaemia (and hypomagnesaemia, hypercalcaemia, renal impairment) potentiates digoxin toxicity; severe toxicity is treated with digoxin-specific Fab fragments.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with extensive anterior STEMI has BP 75/50 mmHg, cold clammy extremities, oliguria and lactate 5 mmol/L. What is the most important intervention to improve survival?
o: Emergency revascularisation (PCI) of the culprit artery
Intra-aortic balloon pump routinely without revascularisation
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Early revascularisation (SHOCK trial) improves survival; routine IABP did not (IABP-SHOCK II). Inotropes/vasopressors are supportive.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient on long-term amiodarone requires monitoring of which organ functions?
o: Thyroid, liver and lungs (TFTs, LFTs, chest X-ray/PFTs)
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Amiodarone causes hypo/hyperthyroidism, hepatotoxicity, pulmonary fibrosis, photosensitivity, slate-grey skin, corneal deposits and optic neuropathy.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 72-year-old woman with hypertension and diabetes has non-valvular atrial fibrillation. What is her CHA₂DS₂-VASc score and recommendation?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Age 65–74 (1) + female (1) + hypertension (1) + diabetes (1) = 4. Anticoagulation recommended for score ≥2 in men and ≥3 in women.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 40-year-old woman with moderate rheumatic mitral stenosis develops atrial fibrillation. Which anticoagulant is recommended?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: DOACs are not recommended in AF with moderate–severe mitral stenosis or mechanical valves (INVICTUS trial favoured VKA in rheumatic AF).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 68-year-old man has AF with ventricular rate 130/min, BP 130/80 mmHg and LVEF 60%. Symptoms began 3 weeks ago. What is the first-line rate-control drug?
o: Digoxin as sole first-line in active patients
Beta-blocker (e.g., bisoprolol) or rate-limiting calcium channel blocker
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Beta-blockers or diltiazem/verapamil (if LVEF preserved) for rate control; cardioversion after 48 hours requires 3 weeks of anticoagulation or TOE.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 25-year-old man has an irregular broad-complex tachycardia at 240/min with varying QRS morphology. Baseline ECG showed a short PR and delta waves. Which drug must be AVOIDED?
o: Verapamil (and other AV nodal blockers such as digoxin, adenosine)
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Pre-excited AF: AV nodal blockers enhance accessory pathway conduction and may precipitate VF; unstable patients need DC cardioversion; definitive treatment is ablation.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old woman has a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 180/min, BP 120/80 mmHg. Vagal manoeuvres fail. What is the next step?
o: IV adenosine 6 mg rapid bolus followed by saline flush (then 12 mg if needed)
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Stable re-entrant SVT: modified Valsalva, then adenosine; verapamil is an alternative (avoid in asthma for adenosine).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 60-year-old post-MI patient has a regular broad-complex tachycardia at 170/min, BP 70/40 mmHg and is confused. What is the immediate treatment?
o: IV amiodarone over 24 hours without cardioversion
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Unstable tachyarrhythmia (shock, syncope, ischaemia, heart failure) requires synchronised cardioversion.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient on haloperidol and ciprofloxacin develops polymorphic VT with twisting QRS around the baseline. ECG before showed QTc 560 ms. What is the first-line drug treatment?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Torsades: IV magnesium, correct K+, stop QT-prolonging drugs; overdrive pacing or isoprenaline for recurrence.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 75-year-old man with syncope has an ECG showing regular P waves and regular broad QRS complexes at 35/min with no relationship between them. What is the definitive treatment?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Complete (third-degree) heart block: atropine/isoprenaline/transcutaneous pacing as bridge; permanent pacemaker definitive.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which ECG pattern is most likely to progress to complete heart block and warrants pacing?
o: Mobitz type II second-degree AV block
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Mobitz II (constant PR with dropped beats) is infranodal and unpredictable; Wenckebach (progressive PR prolongation) is usually benign.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with CKD has K⁺ 7.4 mmol/L and ECG shows tall tented T waves and widened QRS. What is the FIRST treatment?
o: IV calcium gluconate 10% 30 mL (or calcium chloride) to stabilise the myocardium
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Calcium protects the myocardium within minutes but doesn't lower K⁺; then insulin–glucose, salbutamol, and remove K⁺ (binders, dialysis).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: During CPR for ventricular fibrillation, after the third shock, which drugs should be given according to ALS guidelines?
o: Adrenaline 1 mg IV and amiodarone 300 mg IV
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Shockable rhythm: adrenaline 1 mg and amiodarone 300 mg after the 3rd shock; adrenaline every 3–5 minutes; amiodarone 150 mg after 5th shock.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient in cardiac arrest has organised electrical activity on the monitor but no pulse. Which of the following is the priority besides CPR and adrenaline?
o: Search for and treat reversible causes (4 Hs and 4 Ts)
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: PEA is non-shockable; causes: hypoxia, hypovolaemia, hypo/hyperkalaemia/metabolic, hypothermia; thrombosis, tamponade, toxins, tension pneumothorax.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: What is the recommended chest compression rate and depth for adult CPR?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: High-quality CPR: 100–120/min, 5–6 cm, full recoil, minimal interruptions, ratio 30:2 without advanced airway.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old woman from rural Sindh has exertional dyspnoea and haemoptysis. There is a loud first heart sound, opening snap and low-pitched mid-diastolic rumbling murmur at the apex. What is the most common cause?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Rheumatic MS remains common in Pakistan; shorter A2–OS interval indicates more severe stenosis.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with symptomatic severe mitral stenosis (valve area 0.9 cm²) has pliable non-calcified leaflets, no left atrial thrombus and mild MR. What is the preferred intervention?
o: Closed surgical commissurotomy in all cases
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: PBMV is preferred when valve morphology is favourable (Wilkins score ≤8) without LA thrombus or more than mild MR.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 72-year-old man has exertional syncope and angina. There is an ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids, soft S2 and slow-rising pulse. Echo shows mean gradient 48 mmHg and valve area 0.8 cm². What is the management?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Symptomatic severe AS has poor prognosis without intervention; vasodilators are hazardous. TAVI vs SAVR depends on age and surgical risk.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 35-year-old man has a collapsing pulse, wide pulse pressure, visible carotid pulsations and head nodding. Which murmur is expected?
o: Ejection systolic murmur at the right second intercostal space
Pansystolic murmur at apex radiating to axilla
Early diastolic decrescendo murmur at the left sternal edge, best heard leaning forward in expiration
Mid-diastolic murmur at apex with opening snap
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Signs of AR include Corrigan's, de Musset's, Quincke's, Duroziez's; Austin Flint murmur is a mid-diastolic apical rumble.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which murmur is characteristic of chronic mitral regurgitation?
o: Pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla
Continuous murmur below the left clavicle
Ejection systolic murmur radiating to the neck
Early diastolic murmur at left sternal edge
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Chronic MR: soft S1, pansystolic apical murmur radiating to axilla, S3; displaced apex beat.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 40-year-old with poor dental hygiene and rheumatic MR has fever for 4 weeks, splinter haemorrhages and a new murmur. Which organism is most likely?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Subacute native valve IE after dental disease: viridans streptococci; IV drug users: S. aureus (tricuspid); early prosthetic valve: S. epidermidis; colorectal cancer: S. gallolyticus (bovis).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: In suspected infective endocarditis, what is the most important step before starting antibiotics in a stable patient?
o: At least three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Three sets taken at different times (ideally before antibiotics) plus echocardiography (TTE then TOE) are key modified Duke major criteria.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which is an indication for urgent surgery in infective endocarditis?
o: Fever persisting 24 hours after starting antibiotics
Heart failure due to severe valve regurgitation
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Surgery indications: heart failure, uncontrolled infection (abscess, persistent bacteraemia, fungal/resistant organisms) and prevention of embolism (large vegetations >10 mm with emboli).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which patient should receive antibiotic prophylaxis before a dental extraction according to ESC/AHA guidelines?
o: A patient with a prosthetic heart valve
A patient with mitral valve prolapse without regurgitation
A patient with a permanent pacemaker only
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Highest-risk groups: prosthetic valves/repair material, previous IE, certain congenital heart disease (unrepaired cyanotic, recently repaired with prosthetic material).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 45-year-old with a mechanical mitral valve replacement asks which anticoagulant to use long term. What is the correct answer?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: DOACs are contraindicated with mechanical valves (RE-ALIGN trial showed harm); mitral mechanical valves need higher INR targets than aortic.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 50-year-old South Asian man without diabetes or CKD has clinic BP 160/100 mmHg confirmed by ambulatory monitoring. What is a suitable first-line drug?
o: ACE inhibitor or ARB (or calcium channel blocker), ideally as a single-pill combination when BP is this high
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: ESC 2024/ISH: start most patients with dual combination (RAS blocker + CCB or thiazide-like diuretic) in a single pill; NICE uses ACEi/ARB for under-55 non-Black patients.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient has BP 155/95 mmHg despite adherence to optimal doses of amlodipine, perindopril and indapamide. Potassium is 4.0 mmol/L. What is the recommended fourth-line drug?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: PATHWAY-2: spironolactone is most effective in resistant hypertension; screen for primary aldosteronism and exclude pseudo-resistance.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 45-year-old has BP 230/140 mmHg, severe headache, papilloedema and haematuria with AKI. How should BP be lowered?
o: Oral amlodipine and review in 1 week
IV labetalol or nicardipine to reduce mean arterial pressure by no more than 25% in the first hour
Sublingual nifedipine to normalise BP within 10 minutes
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Rapid overcorrection causes cerebral, coronary and renal ischaemia; exceptions include aortic dissection (systolic <120 mmHg within 20 min).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 25-year-old man has sharp chest pain relieved by sitting forward, a pericardial rub and ECG showing widespread concave (saddle-shaped) ST elevation with PR depression. What is the first-line treatment?
o: NSAID (ibuprofen or aspirin) plus colchicine for 3 months
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Colchicine reduces recurrence; steroids are second-line (increase recurrence). In Pakistan, consider TB if effusion persists.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with a known pericardial effusion has hypotension, raised JVP, muffled heart sounds and a fall in systolic BP of 15 mmHg on inspiration. What is the immediate treatment?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Beck's triad and pulsus paradoxus; echo shows diastolic RV collapse. Diuretics and vasodilators worsen tamponade.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 40-year-old man treated for TB pericarditis has ascites, oedema, raised JVP that rises on inspiration, and a pericardial knock. CT shows pericardial calcification. What is the sign of JVP rising with inspiration called?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Kussmaul's sign occurs in constrictive pericarditis, restrictive cardiomyopathy and RV infarction; treatment is pericardiectomy.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 19-year-old athlete collapses while running. His brother died suddenly at 25. There is an ejection systolic murmur at the left sternal edge that increases on standing from squatting and on Valsalva. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Reduced preload (standing, Valsalva) increases LVOT obstruction and the murmur; AS murmur decreases. Avoid dehydration, vasodilators and inotropes; ICD for high SCD risk.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with symptomatic obstructive HCM has LVOT gradient 70 mmHg. Which drug class is first-line?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Beta-blockers (or verapamil) reduce obstruction; mavacamten (cardiac myosin inhibitor) or septal reduction for refractory symptoms.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 28-year-old woman develops breathlessness and oedema 1 month after delivery. Echo shows LVEF 30% with a dilated LV. No previous heart disease. Which drug may be added specifically for this condition?
o: Bromocriptine (with anticoagulation), alongside standard heart failure therapy
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Peripartum cardiomyopathy may be driven by cleaved prolactin; bromocriptine is considered; ACEi are safe postpartum (enalapril/captopril in breastfeeding).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 22-year-old man develops chest pain, raised troponin and new heart failure 1 week after a viral illness. Coronary angiography is normal. Which investigation best supports the diagnosis non-invasively?
o: Cardiac MRI showing myocardial oedema and late gadolinium enhancement
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Cardiac MRI (Lake Louise criteria) supports myocarditis; avoid competitive sport for 3–6 months.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 70-year-old man has heart failure with preserved EF, bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome and low-voltage ECG despite thick LV walls on echo. Which is the likely diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Mismatch of low QRS voltage with increased wall thickness; technetium-PYP scintigraphy diagnoses ATTR; tafamidis improves outcomes.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 55-year-old hypertensive man has sudden tearing chest pain radiating to the back, BP 180/100 mmHg in the right arm and 140/80 in the left. CT shows dissection involving the ascending aorta. What is the management?
o: Emergency surgical repair with IV beta-blocker to control heart rate and BP
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Stanford type A (ascending) requires emergency surgery; type B usually medical (or TEVAR if complicated). Target HR <60 and SBP 100–120.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 45-year-old woman on OCP has sudden pleuritic chest pain and tachycardia. Wells score is 6 (PE likely). She is haemodynamically stable. What is the next investigation?
o: CT pulmonary angiography (with anticoagulation started while awaiting)
D-dimer first and discharge if normal
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: PE likely (Wells >4): proceed to CTPA; D-dimer is used to exclude PE only when PE is unlikely.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with confirmed PE has BP 80/50 mmHg for 20 minutes and a dilated right ventricle on echo. There are no contraindications. What is the treatment of choice?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: High-risk (massive) PE with shock: systemic thrombolysis; catheter-directed or surgical embolectomy if contraindicated.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which ECG finding is most common in acute pulmonary embolism?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Sinus tachycardia is the commonest finding; S1Q3T3, RBBB and right axis deviation are classical but uncommon.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 55-year-old man with established coronary artery disease has LDL-C 110 mg/dL on atorvastatin 80 mg. What is the ESC target and next step?
o: LDL-C <55 mg/dL (1.4 mmol/L) with ≥50% reduction; add ezetimibe
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Very high-risk patients: LDL <55 mg/dL; add ezetimibe, then PCSK9 inhibitor/inclisiran if still above target.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 35-year-old woman has exertional dyspnoea and palpitations. Examination shows fixed wide splitting of S2 and an ejection systolic murmur in the pulmonary area. ECG shows RBBB with right axis deviation. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Fixed splitting of S2 is characteristic of ASD; the systolic murmur is due to increased flow across the pulmonary valve (not flow across the defect).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old with an uncorrected VSD now has central cyanosis, clubbing, a loud P2 and the murmur has disappeared. What has happened?
o: Reversal of shunt to right-to-left due to pulmonary vascular disease (Eisenmenger syndrome)
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Eisenmenger syndrome makes defect closure contraindicated; pregnancy carries very high maternal mortality; pulmonary vasodilators may help.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 20-year-old man has hypertension in the arms, weak delayed femoral pulses (radio-femoral delay) and rib notching on chest X-ray. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Rib notching is due to collateral intercostal arteries; associations include bicuspid aortic valve, Turner syndrome and berry aneurysms.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 25-year-old woman faints while standing in a hot queue after prodromal nausea, sweating and blurred vision, and recovers quickly without confusion. ECG and examination are normal. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Reflex syncope has triggers and prodrome with rapid recovery; red flags are exertional syncope, palpitations, family history of sudden death or abnormal ECG.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 16-year-old girl has recurrent syncope when startled by an alarm clock. ECG shows QTc 520 ms. What is the first-line treatment?
o: Non-selective beta-blocker (nadolol or propranolol) and avoidance of QT-prolonging drugs
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Congenital long QT (LQT2 triggered by auditory stimuli, LQT1 by exercise/swimming); ICD for high-risk patients.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 35-year-old man has syncope at night. ECG shows coved ST elevation in V1–V2 with RBBB-like pattern. Fever unmasks the pattern. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Brugada syndrome (SCN5A sodium channel) causes VF and sudden death; ICD for those with arrhythmic syncope; treat fever promptly.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which ECG criterion suggests left ventricular hypertrophy?
o: S wave in V1 + R wave in V5 or V6 >35 mm (Sokolow–Lyon)
P wave >2.5 mm in lead II
Q waves in II, III, aVF
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Sokolow–Lyon voltage criteria; strain pattern with ST depression/T inversion in lateral leads supports LVH. Tall R in V1 suggests RVH or posterior MI.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with chest pain has ST depression in V1–V3 with tall R waves and upright T waves. What is the most appropriate next step?
o: Treat as unstable angina with no reperfusion
Record posterior leads V7–V9 to look for ST elevation (posterior STEMI) and treat as STEMI if present
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Reciprocal changes in V1–V3 reflect posterior wall infarction, often due to circumflex or RCA occlusion.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 35-year-old woman has progressive exertional dyspnoea, loud P2, parasternal heave and raised JVP with prominent a waves. Echo shows estimated PASP 70 mmHg with normal left heart. Which test is required to confirm the diagnosis?
o: Right heart catheterisation showing mean pulmonary artery pressure >20 mmHg with PVR >2 Wood units
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Right heart catheterisation is the gold standard; classify WHO groups 1–5 and exclude chronic thromboembolic disease with V/Q scan.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 14-year-old boy has migratory polyarthritis of large joints, fever and a new apical pansystolic murmur 3 weeks after a sore throat. ASO titre is raised. What is the recommended secondary prophylaxis?
o: Benzathine penicillin G 1.2 million units IM every 3–4 weeks
Oral amoxicillin only during sore throat episodes
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: With carditis and residual valve disease, prophylaxis continues for 10 years or until age 40 (whichever is longer), sometimes lifelong.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which of the following is a MAJOR modified Jones criterion for acute rheumatic fever?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Major: carditis, arthritis (polyarthritis; monoarthritis/polyarthralgia in moderate/high-risk populations), chorea, erythema marginatum, subcutaneous nodules. Diagnosis requires evidence of preceding GAS infection.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 25-year-old thin woman has atypical chest pain and palpitations. There is a mid-systolic click followed by a late systolic murmur that moves earlier on standing. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: MVP murmur and click occur earlier with reduced preload; associated with connective tissue disorders.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: An intravenous drug user has fever, giant V waves in the JVP, pulsatile liver, and a pansystolic murmur at the lower left sternal edge that increases on inspiration. What is the valve lesion?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Right-sided murmurs increase with inspiration (Carvallo's sign); septic pulmonary emboli are common in right-sided IE.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 65-year-old diabetic presents with epigastric discomfort and sweating for 1 hour. First ECG is normal. What is the most appropriate step?
o: Exercise stress test in the emergency room
Serial ECGs and high-sensitivity troponin at 0 and 1–3 hours
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Diabetics and elderly may present atypically; a normal initial ECG does not exclude ACS; use 0/1-h or 0/3-h hs-troponin algorithms.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 75-year-old obese hypertensive woman has dyspnoea, oedema, raised NT-proBNP and LVEF 58% with diastolic dysfunction. Besides diuretics, which drug class has shown reduction in HF hospitalisation?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: EMPEROR-Preserved and DELIVER trials showed SGLT2 inhibitors reduce HF events in HFpEF.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Ivabradine can be added in HFrEF when resting sinus rate remains above which threshold despite maximal tolerated beta-blocker?
o: ≥70 beats per minute in sinus rhythm
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Ivabradine inhibits the If current in the SA node; ineffective in AF.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 60-year-old with ischaemic cardiomyopathy has LVEF 30% after 3 months of optimal medical therapy and QRS 160 ms with LBBB. What device is indicated?
o: Left ventricular assist device as first option
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: CRT for LVEF ≤35% with LBBB QRS ≥150 ms improves symptoms and survival; ICD for primary prevention of sudden death.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old man has an ejection click and ejection systolic murmur. Echo shows a bicuspid aortic valve. Which associated condition should be screened for?
o: Dilatation of the ascending aorta (aortopathy) and coarctation
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Bicuspid aortic valve (1–2% population) is associated with aortic dilatation/dissection and coarctation; first-degree relatives should be screened.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which score is used to assess bleeding risk in a patient with atrial fibrillation being considered for anticoagulation?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: HAS-BLED ≥3 indicates high bleeding risk; it should prompt correction of modifiable factors, not withholding anticoagulation.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient on simvastatin complains of symmetrical proximal muscle aches. CK is normal. What is the appropriate step?
o: Stop statin permanently and never rechallenge
Consider temporary stop and rechallenge, or switch to a different statin/lower dose
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Statin-associated muscle symptoms with normal CK are managed with rechallenge or alternative statin; CK >10× ULN requires stopping.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 32-year-old woman has resistant hypertension, K⁺ 3.0 mmol/L off diuretics and metabolic alkalosis. What is the most appropriate screening test?
o: Renal artery Doppler as first test
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Primary aldosteronism is the commonest cause of secondary hypertension; hypokalaemia occurs in a minority.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 70-year-old smoker with peripheral vascular disease starts ramipril and his creatinine rises by 40% within 2 weeks. He has an abdominal bruit. What is the likely diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: ACEi/ARB reduce efferent arteriolar tone, dropping GFR in bilateral RAS; atherosclerotic RAS in elderly, fibromuscular dysplasia in young women.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with endocarditis has repeatedly negative blood cultures. She keeps goats and drinks raw milk. Which organism should be considered?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Culture-negative IE: prior antibiotics, HACEK, Coxiella, Bartonella, Brucella, Tropheryma whipplei; serology/PCR needed.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which peripheral sign of infective endocarditis is a painless, flat haemorrhagic lesion on the palms and soles?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Osler's nodes are painful nodules on finger pulps (immune complex); Janeway lesions are painless (septic microemboli); Roth spots are retinal.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: An ECG shows regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 150/min with a "saw-tooth" baseline in leads II, III and aVF. What is the definitive treatment for recurrent typical flutter?
o: Catheter ablation of the cavotricuspid isthmus
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Atrial rate ~300/min with 2:1 block gives ventricular rate 150/min; anticoagulation like AF; CTI ablation has high success.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient has sinus bradycardia of 35/min with BP 80/50 mmHg and dizziness. What is the first drug to give?
o: IV atropine 500 micrograms, repeated to maximum 3 mg
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: If atropine fails: isoprenaline/adrenaline infusion or transcutaneous pacing; atropine is ineffective in heart transplant patients.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient in Pakistan has a large pericardial effusion with lymphocytic exudate and high adenosine deaminase. What is the most likely cause?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: In TB-endemic areas, TB is the leading cause of large pericardial effusion; ADA >40 U/L supports; ATT for 6 months, constriction is a complication.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with angina taking sildenafil for erectile dysfunction presents with chest pain. Which drug must be avoided within 24–48 hours of sildenafil?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: PDE5 inhibitors potentiate nitrates causing profound hypotension.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which pharmacotherapy is most effective for smoking cessation in a patient with coronary disease?
o: Nicotine replacement is contraindicated after MI
Bupropion is contraindicated in all cardiac patients
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Varenicline and combination NRT are most effective; NRT is safe in stable cardiovascular disease.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient found outdoors in winter has core temperature 29°C. ECG shows bradycardia and a positive deflection at the J point. What is this wave called?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Osborn waves occur in hypothermia; epsilon waves in ARVC; U waves in hypokalaemia; delta waves in WPW.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which ECG change is most characteristic of hypokalaemia?
o: Prominent U waves with T-wave flattening and ST depression
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Hypokalaemia prolongs repolarisation and causes U waves; hyperkalaemia produces tented T waves.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 40-year-old man has a first DVT after a long-haul flight and knee surgery (provoked). How long should he be anticoagulated?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Provoked VTE with transient risk factor: 3 months; unprovoked VTE: consider extended therapy.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 45-year-old man who drinks heavily has progressive heart failure. Echo shows a globally dilated, poorly contracting LV with no coronary disease. What is the most important intervention?
o: Complete abstinence from alcohol with guideline-directed HF therapy
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy may improve markedly with abstinence; thiamine deficiency (wet beriberi) should also be considered.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which symptom in aortic stenosis carries the WORST prognosis without valve replacement?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Average survival: angina ~5 years, syncope ~3 years, heart failure ~2 years without intervention.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 40-year-old woman has episodic dyspnoea on lying on her left side, fever, weight loss, and a "tumour plop" in early diastole. Echo shows a pedunculated mass attached to the interatrial septum. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Myxoma is the commonest primary cardiac tumour in adults; constitutional symptoms due to IL-6; treat by surgical excision.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 25-year-old woman with asthma has PEF 40% of best, cannot complete sentences, RR 28/min, HR 118/min and SpO₂ 93%. What is the immediate treatment?
o: Oxygen to SpO₂ 93–95%, nebulised salbutamol (oxygen-driven) with ipratropium, and oral prednisolone 40–50 mg
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: BTS/GINA: acute severe asthma (PEF 33–50%); add IV magnesium sulphate if poor response. Sedation is contraindicated.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which finding indicates LIFE-THREATENING asthma?
o: Normal PaCO₂ (4.6–6.0 kPa) in a breathless asthmatic, or a silent chest
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Life-threatening features: PEF <33%, SpO₂ <92%, PaO₂ <8 kPa, normal PaCO₂, silent chest, cyanosis, exhaustion, arrhythmia, hypotension, altered consciousness. Raised PaCO₂ = near-fatal.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old with asthma has symptoms 3 times per week and nocturnal waking once a week despite as-needed salbutamol. According to GINA Track 1, what is the preferred treatment?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: GINA advises against SABA-only treatment; ICS-formoterol reduces severe exacerbations. LABA without ICS increases asthma mortality.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which spirometry finding supports a diagnosis of asthma in an adult with episodic wheeze?
o: Fixed obstruction not reversible with bronchodilator
Increase in FEV₁ ≥12% and ≥200 mL after bronchodilator
FEV₁/FVC ratio of 0.85 with reduced FVC
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Significant bronchodilator reversibility, PEF variability >10%, raised FeNO or positive challenge test support asthma.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 62-year-old smoker (40 pack-years) has chronic cough and breathlessness. Which spirometry result confirms COPD?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Persistent airflow limitation after bronchodilator defines COPD; FEV₁ % predicted grades severity (GOLD 1–4).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A COPD patient has increased breathlessness and purulent sputum. ABG on 28% O₂: pH 7.29, PaCO₂ 62 mmHg, PaO₂ 58 mmHg, HCO₃⁻ 30 mmol/L. After initial nebulisers and steroids, what is the next step?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Acute hypercapnic respiratory acidosis (pH <7.35, PaCO₂ >45) in COPD exacerbation is an indication for NIV; target SpO₂ 88–92%.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Why should oxygen saturation be targeted at 88–92% in a patient with COPD and chronic CO₂ retention?
o: Excess oxygen worsens V/Q mismatch and reduces respiratory drive, causing hypercapnic acidosis
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Uncontrolled oxygen in CO₂ retainers (loss of hypoxic vasoconstriction, Haldane effect) leads to rising PaCO₂.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which COPD patient meets criteria for long-term oxygen therapy?
o: PaO₂ 9.5 kPa with no other features
PaO₂ 7.0 kPa (53 mmHg) on air at rest on two occasions 3 weeks apart, non-smoker
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: LTOT (≥15 h/day) if PaO₂ <7.3 kPa, or 7.3–8 kPa with polycythaemia, pulmonary hypertension or peripheral oedema; smoking is a fire hazard contraindication.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A COPD patient (GOLD group E) with 2 exacerbations last year and blood eosinophils 350 cells/µL is on LAMA+LABA. What should be added?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: GOLD: add ICS if exacerbations with eosinophils ≥300 (or ≥100 with persistent exacerbations); consider roflumilast or azithromycin otherwise.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 70-year-old man with pneumonia is confused, urea 9 mmol/L, RR 32/min and BP 95/55 mmHg. What is his CURB-65 score and management?
o: 5; severe pneumonia – hospital admission and consider ICU
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Confusion, Urea >7, RR ≥30, BP (SBP <90 or DBP ≤60), age ≥65 = 5. Score 3–5 severe; IV co-amoxiclav + macrolide.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old plumber has high fever, dry cough, confusion, diarrhoea, hyponatraemia and deranged LFTs after working on a hotel cooling tower. Which test is useful for rapid diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Legionella pneumophila serogroup 1 urine antigen; treat with macrolide or fluoroquinolone.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 19-year-old student has gradual-onset dry cough, headache, bilateral patchy infiltrates, erythema multiforme and haemolytic anaemia. What is the likely organism?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Mycoplasma causes cold agglutinin haemolysis and erythema multiforme; beta-lactams are ineffective (no cell wall); use macrolide/doxycycline.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: An alcoholic man has sudden-onset fever with thick "red currant jelly" sputum and upper lobe consolidation with bulging fissure. What is the likely organism?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Klebsiella affects alcoholics and diabetics, causing cavitation and abscess formation.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with a stroke and dysphagia develops pneumonia. Which lung segment is most commonly involved if aspiration occurred while supine?
o: Anterior segment of left upper lobe
Posterior segment of right upper lobe or apical segment of right lower lobe
Left lower lobe basal segments while upright
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Right main bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical; supine aspiration affects posterior segments; upright affects right lower basal segments.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A man with poor dentition and alcohol misuse has fever, foul-smelling sputum and a thick-walled cavity with air–fluid level. What is the treatment?
o: Prolonged antibiotics covering anaerobes (e.g., co-amoxiclav or clindamycin) with postural drainage
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Most lung abscesses respond to 4–6 weeks of antibiotics; exclude underlying carcinoma/obstruction by bronchoscopy if no response.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old from a TB-endemic area has cough for 5 weeks, haemoptysis, night sweats and weight loss. What is the WHO-recommended initial diagnostic test?
o: Rapid molecular test on sputum (Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra)
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: WHO recommends rapid molecular tests as initial diagnostic tests; they also detect rifampicin resistance. TST/IGRA do not distinguish latent from active TB.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: What is the standard treatment for new drug-susceptible pulmonary TB in adults?
o: 2 months of isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, followed by 4 months of isoniazid and rifampicin
2 months of streptomycin and isoniazid only
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: 2HRZE/4HR is standard; a 4-month rifapentine–moxifloxacin regimen is an alternative for eligible patients aged ≥12.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient on ATT complains of reduced red–green colour discrimination and blurred vision. Which drug is responsible?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Ethambutol optic neuritis; isoniazid – peripheral neuropathy (prevent with pyridoxine) and hepatitis; rifampicin – orange secretions, enzyme induction; pyrazinamide – hepatotoxicity, hyperuricaemia.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Four weeks into ATT, a patient develops jaundice with ALT 450 U/L (normal <40). What is the correct action?
o: Continue all drugs and add silymarin
Stop hepatotoxic drugs (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide) and reintroduce sequentially once LFTs normalise
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: ALT >5× ULN (or >3× with symptoms/jaundice) requires stopping; if unwell, give non-hepatotoxic cover (ethambutol, levofloxacin, amikacin).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A woman on combined oral contraceptive pill starts rifampicin-based TB treatment. What advice is correct?
o: Rifampicin increases OCP levels, causing thrombosis
Double the OCP dose is the only option
Use alternative/additional contraception because rifampicin induces liver enzymes and reduces OCP efficacy
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Rifampicin (CYP450 inducer) reduces levels of OCP, warfarin, steroids, antiretrovirals and many other drugs; copper IUD or DMPA is preferred.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient's Xpert test shows MTB detected with rifampicin resistance. What is the WHO-preferred regimen for most patients with MDR/RR-TB?
o: Add a single second-line drug to the failing regimen
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: WHO recommends all-oral shorter regimens (BPaLM) for MDR/RR-TB; never add a single drug to a failing regimen.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 28-year-old man has a unilateral lymphocytic exudative pleural effusion with low glucose and adenosine deaminase 70 U/L. Sputum is negative. What is the most likely cause?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: In TB-endemic areas, lymphocytic exudate with high ADA (>40 U/L) is strongly suggestive; pleural biopsy has the highest yield.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which result indicates that a pleural effusion is an exudate by Light's criteria?
o: Pleural fluid LDH less than 2/3 upper limit of serum LDH
Pleural protein 20 g/L with serum protein 70 g/L and normal LDH
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Exudate if any: protein ratio >0.5, LDH ratio >0.6, pleural LDH >2/3 of upper normal serum LDH.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with pneumonia has persistent fever and a pleural collection with pH 7.0 and glucose 30 mg/dL. What is the management?
o: Chest tube drainage with IV antibiotics
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Complicated parapneumonic effusion (pH <7.2) or frank pus requires drainage; intrapleural tPA–DNase or VATS if loculated.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A tall 22-year-old smoker has sudden pleuritic chest pain. X-ray shows a 3 cm rim of air at the hilum level. He is not breathless. What is the management according to BTS 2023?
o: Pleurodesis at first episode in all
Conservative management with outpatient review (or ambulatory drainage) since he is minimally symptomatic
Immediate intercostal drain in all cases
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: BTS 2023 focuses on symptoms rather than size; conservative management for minimally symptomatic PSP; smoking cessation.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 65-year-old with COPD develops a pneumothorax with 2.5 cm rim and breathlessness. What is the management?
o: Admit and insert a chest drain
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Secondary pneumothorax (underlying lung disease) is less well tolerated; usually needs admission and drainage.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 45-year-old has daily copious purulent sputum, recurrent chest infections and coarse crackles. What is the investigation of choice for diagnosis?
o: High-resolution CT chest showing airway dilatation (signet ring sign)
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: HRCT: bronchoarterial ratio >1, lack of tapering; investigate causes (post-TB, ABPA, immunodeficiency, CF, PCD).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: An asthmatic has worsening control, fleeting pulmonary infiltrates, brownish mucus plugs, eosinophilia and total IgE >1000 IU/mL. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: ABPA: central bronchiectasis, positive Aspergillus-specific IgE/IgG; treated with oral steroids ± itraconazole.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with old healed TB cavity has recurrent haemoptysis. CT shows a mobile round mass within the cavity with an air crescent. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Aspergilloma colonises pre-existing cavities; massive haemoptysis may require bronchial artery embolisation or surgery.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with bronchiectasis coughs up 300 mL of blood. SpO₂ is 90%. Which position should the patient be placed in?
o: Lying on the side of the bleeding lung (bleeding side down)
Lying on the side of the healthy lung
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Keeps blood from spilling into the healthy lung; secure airway, then bronchoscopy and bronchial artery embolisation.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 68-year-old man has progressive dyspnoea, dry cough, clubbing and fine "velcro" basal crackles. HRCT shows subpleural basal honeycombing (UIP pattern). What treatment slows disease progression?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: PANTHER-IPF showed harm with triple therapy; antifibrotics slow FVC decline. Spirometry shows restrictive pattern with low DLCO.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old woman has erythema nodosum, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, fever and arthralgia. Serum ACE and calcium are raised. What is this presentation called and its prognosis?
o: Löfgren syndrome; excellent prognosis with spontaneous remission
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Löfgren syndrome usually resolves spontaneously; NSAIDs for symptoms. Exclude TB and lymphoma in Pakistan.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A pigeon breeder has fever, cough and dyspnoea 6 hours after cleaning lofts, with bilateral ground-glass opacities. What is the most important management step?
o: Avoid antigen exposure (with steroids if severe)
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis (bird fancier's lung) is type III/IV reaction; chronic exposure leads to fibrosis.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A former shipyard worker has chest pain, weight loss and a unilateral pleural effusion with nodular pleural thickening encasing the lung. What is the most likely diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Mesothelioma latency is 30–40 years; diagnosis by CT-guided or thoracoscopic pleural biopsy; poor prognosis.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A stone crusher worker has progressive dyspnoea. Chest X-ray shows upper zone nodules and "egg-shell" calcification of hilar nodes. Which infection is he at increased risk of?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Silica impairs macrophage function; silicosis greatly increases TB risk; common among stone-crushing and mining workers in Pakistan.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 60-year-old smoker has a central lung mass, confusion and serum sodium 118 mmol/L with high urine osmolality and euvolaemia. What is the likely cause of hyponatraemia?
o: SIADH due to small cell lung carcinoma
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: SCLC: SIADH, ectopic ACTH, Lambert–Eaton syndrome. Squamous: PTHrP hypercalcaemia. Adenocarcinoma: most common in non-smokers, EGFR mutations.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 58-year-old smoker has severe shoulder pain radiating down the inner arm, wasting of small hand muscles and ipsilateral ptosis and miosis. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Apical tumour invades brachial plexus (C8–T1) and sympathetic chain (Horner's syndrome).

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with lung cancer has facial swelling, dilated chest wall veins and breathlessness worse lying down. What is the initial management for symptomatic relief in most cases?
o: Immediate surgery to remove the tumour
Endovascular stenting with steroids (and tissue diagnosis-directed chemo/radiotherapy)
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Stenting gives rapid relief; SCLC and lymphoma respond well to chemotherapy.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 45-year-old non-smoking woman has metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with an EGFR exon 19 deletion. What is the preferred first-line treatment?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Molecular testing (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, KRAS, PD-L1) guides treatment of advanced NSCLC.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: An obese man snores loudly, has witnessed apnoeas, daytime sleepiness (Epworth score 16) and resistant hypertension. Polysomnography shows AHI 35/hour. What is the treatment of choice?
o: Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) with weight reduction
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Severe OSA (AHI ≥30) is treated with CPAP; advise on driving safety; avoid alcohol/sedatives.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient has pH 7.50, PaCO₂ 25 mmHg, PaO₂ 60 mmHg and HCO₃⁻ 22 mmol/L. What is the interpretation?
o: Acute respiratory alkalosis with hypoxaemia (e.g., pulmonary embolism)
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: High pH with low PaCO₂ and normal bicarbonate indicates uncompensated respiratory alkalosis; hypoxaemia drives hyperventilation.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which condition typically causes type 2 (hypercapnic) respiratory failure?
o: Lobar pneumonia in a young adult
Guillain–Barré syndrome with respiratory muscle weakness
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Type 2 failure (PaCO₂ >50 mmHg) results from alveolar hypoventilation: COPD, neuromuscular disease, chest wall deformity, sedative overdose. Monitor FVC in GBS.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with severe pancreatitis has bilateral infiltrates within 1 week of insult, PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio of 120 on PEEP 10, and no cardiac failure. What ventilation strategy improves survival?
o: Low tidal volume ventilation (6 mL/kg predicted body weight) with plateau pressure <30 cmH₂O, and prone positioning for severe ARDS
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Berlin: PaO₂/FiO₂ ≤100 severe, 100–200 moderate, 200–300 mild. ARDSNet and PROSEVA trials guide lung-protective ventilation.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which spirometry pattern indicates restrictive lung disease?
o: Reduced FEV₁ and FVC with normal or increased FEV₁/FVC ratio
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Restrictive: low TLC; causes include ILD, obesity, neuromuscular disease, chest wall deformity. Obstructive: low ratio.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: In which condition is diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) typically INCREASED?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Increased DLCO: alveolar haemorrhage, polycythaemia, asthma, left-to-right shunts. Decreased: emphysema, ILD, PE, anaemia.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: An HIV patient with CD4 count 80 cells/mm³ has progressive dry cough, exertional desaturation and bilateral perihilar ground-glass opacities. What is the treatment?
o: High-dose co-trimoxazole with prednisolone if PaO₂ <70 mmHg
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: PCP treatment: trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole for 21 days; adjunctive steroids for moderate–severe hypoxaemia; start ART within 2 weeks.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 67-year-old with COPD has fever, myalgia and cough during an influenza outbreak, and is admitted within 36 hours of onset. What antiviral is recommended?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Neuraminidase inhibitors reduce complications in high-risk/hospitalised patients; ideally started within 48 hours but still given later in severe disease. Annual vaccination is recommended.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 35-year-old non-smoker has emphysema predominantly in the lower lobes (panacinar) and abnormal liver function tests. What is the likely diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: AATD (PiZZ) causes basal panacinar emphysema and cirrhosis; smoking cessation is critical; augmentation therapy in selected patients.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with late-onset asthma, eosinophilia 25%, sinusitis, peripheral neuropathy and fleeting infiltrates has positive p-ANCA. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: EGPA is a small-vessel vasculitis; mepolizumab is approved; cardiac involvement is the main cause of death.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A shepherd from Balochistan has a well-defined round opacity in the lung. After coughing up salty fluid, X-ray shows a "water lily" sign. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Echinococcus granulosus; floating membrane in cyst (water lily/camalote sign); treated with surgery and albendazole.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A patient with morbid obesity has daytime hypersomnolence, PaCO₂ 52 mmHg on awake ABG, and no other lung disease. What is the diagnosis?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: OHS: BMI ≥30 with daytime hypercapnia (PaCO₂ >45 mmHg) after excluding other causes; treated with NIV/CPAP and weight loss.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A healthcare worker has a positive IGRA, no symptoms and normal chest X-ray. Which regimen is recommended for TB preventive treatment?
o: 3 months of weekly isoniazid–rifapentine (3HP) or 3 months of daily isoniazid–rifampicin (3HR), or 6 months isoniazid
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: WHO recommends shorter rifamycin-based TPT regimens; exclude active TB first.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: A 55-year-old man has persistent dry cough 3 weeks after starting lisinopril. Chest X-ray is normal. What is the best management?
o: Switch to an angiotensin receptor blocker
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: ACEi cough (bradykinin accumulation) occurs in 10–15%; ARBs don't cause it; cough may take weeks to resolve after stopping.

cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.s: Which condition is NOT typically associated with digital clubbing?
cardiorespiratory-iii/medicine.e: Clubbing in a COPD patient should prompt search for lung cancer or bronchiectasis.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: A 3-month-old has poor feeding, sweating during feeds, failure to thrive and tachypnoea. There is a harsh pansystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border and hepatomegaly. What is the most likely diagnosis?
o: Large ventricular septal defect with heart failure
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: VSD is the commonest congenital heart disease; large VSD causes heart failure at 6–8 weeks as pulmonary vascular resistance falls.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: A 6-month-old thriving child has a small muscular VSD with a loud murmur and normal heart size. What is the most appropriate advice?
o: Reassurance with follow-up; many close spontaneously
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: Small restrictive VSDs have loud murmurs but little haemodynamic effect; 30–50% close spontaneously. Good dental hygiene is advised.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: A 28-week preterm neonate on day 4 has bounding pulses, wide pulse pressure, a continuous murmur below the left clavicle and increasing ventilatory requirement. Echo confirms a haemodynamically significant PDA. What is the medical treatment?
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: Prostaglandin inhibitors close PDA in preterms; PGE1 keeps the duct open in duct-dependent lesions.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: Which congenital heart lesion is most associated with congenital rubella syndrome?
o: Patent ductus arteriosus (and peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis)
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: Congenital rubella triad: cataract, sensorineural deafness, PDA/PPS.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: A 2-year-old cyanotic child squats after walking. There is an ejection systolic murmur at the left upper sternal border and a single S2. Chest X-ray shows a "boot-shaped" heart with oligaemic lung fields. What determines the degree of cyanosis?
o: Severity of right ventricular outflow tract obstruction
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: TOF: VSD, overriding aorta, RVOTO and RVH; murmur is due to RVOTO (not VSD) and becomes softer during spells.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: A 9-month-old with TOF becomes deeply cyanosed, irritable and hyperpnoeic after crying; the murmur disappears. What is the first step?
o: Knee–chest position, calm the child and give oxygen
Leave supine and perform chest X-ray
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: Then IV morphine, IV fluids, propranolol and phenylephrine if needed; knee-chest increases SVR and reduces right-to-left shunt.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: A term male infant becomes severely cyanosed within hours of birth with no murmur and no respiratory distress. Hyperoxia test fails. Chest X-ray shows "egg on a string". What is the immediate drug?
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: TGA requires mixing via PDA/foramen ovale; balloon atrial septostomy may be needed; arterial switch in the first 2–3 weeks.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: A cyanosed neonate is given 100% oxygen for 10 minutes. Right radial arterial PaO₂ rises from 40 to 250 mmHg. What does this suggest?
o: Pulmonary (parenchymal) cause of cyanosis rather than cyanotic heart disease
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: PaO₂ >150 mmHg on 100% O₂ makes cyanotic CHD unlikely; <100 mmHg suggests a fixed right-to-left shunt.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: A 7-day-old baby presents in shock with poor feeding, grey colour, absent femoral pulses and metabolic acidosis. What is the most important immediate drug?
o: Prostaglandin E1 to reopen the ductus arteriosus
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: Critical coarctation and hypoplastic left heart are duct-dependent systemic circulations; collapse occurs when the duct closes.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: A 2-day-old neonate develops rapid collapse with poor peripheral pulses in all four limbs, tachypnoea and hepatomegaly as the duct closes. Echo shows a tiny left ventricle and atretic aortic valve. What is the eventual surgical pathway?
o: Staged palliation: Norwood, bidirectional Glenn, then Fontan
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: HLHS requires three-stage single-ventricle palliation or cardiac transplantation.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: A 5-year-old asymptomatic girl has an ejection systolic murmur at the upper left sternal edge and fixed split S2. Echo shows a 14 mm secundum ASD with RV dilatation. What is the management?
o: Elective transcatheter device closure (or surgery) at around 3–5 years
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: Significant ASDs (RV volume overload) are closed electively before school age to prevent pulmonary hypertension, arrhythmias and heart failure in adult life.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: Which feature suggests an innocent (functional) murmur in a child?
o: Soft systolic murmur that varies with posture, no thrill, normal S2 and asymptomatic child
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: Innocent murmurs (Still's, venous hum, pulmonary flow) are soft, systolic (except venous hum), short, localised and change with position.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: A 3-year-old has had fever for 6 days with bilateral non-purulent conjunctivitis, red cracked lips, strawberry tongue, polymorphous rash, oedema of hands and cervical lymphadenopathy. What is the most serious complication?
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: Kawasaki disease is the commonest cause of acquired heart disease in children in high-income countries; echocardiography at diagnosis and follow-up.

cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.s: What is the treatment of choice for Kawasaki disease?
o: IVIG 2 g/kg as a single infusion plus aspirin, ideally within 10 days of fever onset
cardiorespiratory-iii/paediatrics.e: IVIG reduces coronary aneurysm risk from ~25% to <5%; steroids are added in high-risk patients; avoid live vaccines for 11 months after IVIG.
