endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/surgery.e: AIs are preferred after menopause (monitor bone density); tamoxifen for premenopausal women; trastuzumab only for HER2-positive disease.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/surgery.s: A woman with a 2 cm invasive breast cancer has a clinically and ultrasound-negative axilla. What is the recommended axillary staging?
o: Axillary lymph node clearance in all cases
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/surgery.e: SLNB (blue dye and/or radioisotope) reduces lymphoedema compared with axillary clearance.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/surgery.s: A 35-year-old woman with a BRCA1 mutation has completed her family. Which option provides the greatest reduction in ovarian cancer risk?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/surgery.e: Ovarian cancer screening is ineffective; RRSO reduces ovarian cancer risk by ~80%.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/surgery.s: A 45-year-old woman has spontaneous single-duct bloody nipple discharge without a palpable lump. Mammography is normal. What is the most likely cause?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/surgery.e: Investigate single-duct bloody discharge with ultrasound ± ductoscopy and microdochectomy to exclude DCIS.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/surgery.s: A 60-year-old woman has a unilateral eczematous lesion that has destroyed the nipple and not responded to topical steroids. What is the next step?
o: Punch biopsy of the nipple and mammography to look for underlying carcinoma
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/surgery.e: Paget's disease starts on the nipple (eczema starts on the areola) and is almost always associated with DCIS or invasive cancer.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/surgery.s: A 3 cm adrenal mass with attenuation of 5 Hounsfield units is found incidentally on CT in a normotensive patient. What further evaluation is required?
o: Hormonal work-up: 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test and plasma metanephrines
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/surgery.e: <10 HU suggests a lipid-rich benign adenoma; add aldosterone–renin ratio if hypertensive or hypokalaemic; surgery for functional or >4 cm/suspicious lesions.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/surgery.s: A 65-year-old woman with a large multinodular goitre develops facial congestion and dyspnoea when raising both arms above her head. What is this sign called?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/surgery.e: Pemberton's sign indicates thoracic inlet obstruction; evaluate with CT and plan thyroidectomy.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.s: A newborn screening test shows TSH 80 mIU/L in an asymptomatic baby. What is the most appropriate step?
o: Confirm with serum TSH/free T4 and start levothyroxine 10–15 mcg/kg/day promptly (within the first 2 weeks)
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.e: Early treatment prevents intellectual disability; clinical signs (prolonged jaundice, umbilical hernia, macroglossia) appear late.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.s: A 2-week-old with ambiguous genitalia presents with vomiting, dehydration, Na⁺ 124 and K⁺ 7.2 mmol/L. Karyotype is 46,XX. Which hormone is markedly raised?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.e: Salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency is treated with hydrocortisone, fludrocortisone and salt; 11β-hydroxylase deficiency causes hypertension.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.s: A 10-year-old being treated for DKA develops headache, bradycardia, rising BP and falling consciousness 6 hours into treatment. What is the likely complication and treatment?
o: Cerebral oedema; IV mannitol (0.5–1 g/kg) or hypertonic saline, and reduce fluid rate
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.e: Cerebral oedema is the leading cause of death in paediatric DKA; avoid insulin boluses and over-rapid fluids; do not delay treatment for imaging.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.s: A 6-year-old girl has breast development, pubic hair, growth acceleration and advanced bone age. LH rises markedly after GnRH stimulation and MRI brain is normal. What is the treatment?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.e: Central precocious puberty is usually idiopathic in girls; boys more often have CNS lesions.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.s: A 14-year-old boy is short with delayed puberty, bone age 11 years, normal growth velocity and a father who was a "late bloomer". What is the diagnosis?
o: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.e: Delayed bone age with normal growth velocity; reassurance, or short-course low-dose testosterone for psychosocial distress.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.s: A macrosomic infant of a diabetic mother is jittery at 2 hours with blood glucose 30 mg/dL. What is the mechanism?
o: Fetal hyperinsulinism from maternal hyperglycaemia persisting after birth
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.e: Glucose (not insulin) crosses the placenta, causing fetal beta-cell hyperplasia; feed early; IV 10% dextrose 2 mL/kg if symptomatic.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.s: A phenotypic female teenager has primary amenorrhoea, normal breast development, scanty pubic hair and a blind-ending vagina. Karyotype is 46,XY. What is the diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.e: Intra-abdominal testes are removed after puberty because of malignancy risk; MRKH is 46,XX with normal pubic hair.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.s: A 7-year-old has polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss and new bedwetting for 3 weeks. Random glucose is 350 mg/dL without ketoacidosis. What is the management?
o: Same-day specialist referral and start of subcutaneous insulin with diabetes education
Wait for HbA1c result next week
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/paediatri.e: Delay in children with suspected type 1 diabetes risks DKA.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A 30-year-old woman with epilepsy on lamotrigine and BMI 32 plans pregnancy. What folic acid dose is recommended before conception?
o: 400 micrograms daily only after a positive pregnancy test
5 mg daily from at least 3 months before conception until 12 weeks
5 mg daily only in the third trimester
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: High-dose folate is advised for antiepileptic use, obesity (BMI ≥30), diabetes, previous neural tube defect, sickle cell or thalassaemia; others take 400 micrograms.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: Which set of investigations is routinely offered at the antenatal booking visit?
o: CBC, blood group and antibody screen, HBsAg, HIV, syphilis serology, urine culture and blood glucose screening
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Also offer haemoglobinopathy screening (thalassaemia carrier status in Pakistan) and dating/anomaly ultrasound.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman with regular 28-day cycles has an LMP of 10 January. What is her expected date of delivery by Naegele's rule?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Naegele's rule: LMP + 7 days − 3 months (+1 year); adjust for cycle length; first-trimester CRL dating is most accurate.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: Which is the recommended first-trimester combined screening test for Down syndrome?
o: Nuchal translucency with serum free β-hCG and PAPP-A at 11–13+6 weeks
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Trisomy 21: raised β-hCG, low PAPP-A, increased NT; cell-free fetal DNA is a highly sensitive screening option; diagnosis requires CVS/amniocentesis.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman at 9 weeks has persistent vomiting, 6% weight loss, ketonuria and Na⁺ 131 mmol/L. What is the first-line management?
o: Stop all oral intake for a week
IV normal saline with potassium, antiemetics (e.g., cyclizine or promethazine) and thiamine supplementation
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Dextrose without thiamine risks Wernicke's encephalopathy; exclude molar and multiple pregnancy by ultrasound; consider thromboprophylaxis.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman at 8 weeks has light vaginal bleeding without pain. The cervical os is closed and ultrasound shows a viable intrauterine pregnancy with fetal heartbeat. What is the diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Threatened: closed os, viable pregnancy; inevitable: open os; incomplete: retained products; missed: non-viable fetus without symptoms.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: Ultrasound at 10 weeks shows a crown–rump length of 12 mm with no fetal heartbeat. The woman is haemodynamically stable. Which medical management is appropriate?
o: Mifepristone 200 mg orally followed 48 hours later by misoprostol 800 micrograms vaginally
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: NICE recommends mifepristone + misoprostol for missed miscarriage; expectant or surgical (MVA) options are also offered.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman has had three consecutive first-trimester miscarriages. Which investigation is most important?
o: Antiphospholipid antibodies (lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, anti-β2GPI) on two occasions
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Also parental karyotype (if fetal tissue abnormal), pelvic ultrasound for uterine anomalies and thyroid function; APS is treated with aspirin + LMWH.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman with 6 weeks of amenorrhoea has lower abdominal pain and spotting. β-hCG is 2,500 IU/L and transvaginal ultrasound shows an empty uterus with an adnexal mass. She is stable. What is the diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: An intrauterine sac should be visible on TVS when β-hCG exceeds ~1,500–2,000 IU/L; ampulla is the commonest site.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: Which woman with ectopic pregnancy is most suitable for methotrexate treatment?
o: β-hCG 8,000 IU/L with fetal cardiac activity
Stable, unruptured, no fetal heartbeat, adnexal mass <35 mm, β-hCG <1,500 IU/L and able to attend follow-up
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Serum β-hCG is checked on days 4 and 7 (≥15% fall expected); avoid pregnancy for 3–6 months after methotrexate.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman with 7 weeks amenorrhoea collapses with severe abdominal pain, shoulder tip pain, pulse 130/min and BP 70/40 mmHg. What is the management?
o: Resuscitation and emergency laparotomy/laparoscopy with salpingectomy
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Haemodynamic instability mandates immediate surgery; salpingectomy is preferred if the contralateral tube is healthy.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman at 12 weeks has vaginal bleeding, hyperemesis, uterus larger than dates and β-hCG 350,000 IU/L. Ultrasound shows a "snowstorm" appearance without a fetus. What is the treatment?
o: Suction evacuation followed by serial β-hCG monitoring
Medical termination with misoprostol as first line
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Complete mole (46,XX paternal); suction curettage is preferred; follow-up hCG until normal; avoid pregnancy until follow-up completed.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: After evacuation of a molar pregnancy, β-hCG plateaus on 4 consecutive weekly measurements. Chest X-ray shows lung nodules. What is the treatment?
o: Chemotherapy (methotrexate for low-risk GTN; EMA-CO for high-risk based on FIGO score)
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: GTN is highly chemosensitive with cure rates approaching 100% for low-risk disease.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: According to NICE/IADPSG criteria, which result on a 75 g OGTT at 26 weeks diagnoses gestational diabetes?
o: Fasting glucose ≥92 mg/dL (5.1 mmol/L) or 1-h ≥180 mg/dL or 2-h ≥153 mg/dL (IADPSG)
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: IADPSG/WHO 2013 thresholds (NICE uses fasting ≥5.6 or 2-h ≥7.8 mmol/L); OGTT at 24–28 weeks, earlier if previous GDM.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman with GDM at 30 weeks has fasting glucose 115 mg/dL despite 2 weeks of diet and exercise. Ultrasound shows fetal abdominal circumference >97th centile. What is the treatment?
o: Start glibenclamide as the only option
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Fasting ≥7 mmol/L (126 mg/dL) at diagnosis or macrosomia warrants insulin; targets fasting <95 mg/dL, 1-h postprandial <140 mg/dL.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman with GDM controlled on diet delivered healthy. What follow-up is recommended?
o: Check glucose only in next pregnancy
Stop treatment after delivery; check fasting glucose/HbA1c/OGTT at 6–13 weeks postpartum, then annual screening
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Women with GDM have up to 50% risk of type 2 diabetes within 10 years.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: Which finding defines pre-eclampsia in a previously normotensive woman at 32 weeks with BP 150/100 mmHg?
o: Weight gain of 2 kg in a week only
New proteinuria (PCR ≥30 mg/mmol) or maternal organ dysfunction (e.g., raised creatinine, liver enzymes, low platelets) or uteroplacental dysfunction
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Pre-eclampsia: new hypertension after 20 weeks plus proteinuria or organ/placental dysfunction (ISSHP). Oedema is no longer a criterion.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: Which woman should be advised to take low-dose aspirin from 12 weeks to reduce pre-eclampsia risk?
o: A woman with iron deficiency only
A woman with a previous caesarean section alone
A healthy multiparous 25-year-old with previous normal pregnancies
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: High risk: previous hypertensive pregnancy disease, CKD, SLE/APS, diabetes, chronic hypertension. Aspirin 75–150 mg at night from 12 weeks until birth (ASPRE).

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman at 34 weeks has BP 170/112 mmHg with headache. What is the first-line antihypertensive for acute control?
o: Oral nifedipine (immediate release) or IV labetalol
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: IV hydralazine is an alternative; ACE inhibitors/ARBs are contraindicated in pregnancy (fetal renal toxicity).

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman with severe pre-eclampsia receiving magnesium sulphate has absent patellar reflexes and respiratory rate 9/min. What is the immediate action?
o: Stop the magnesium infusion and give IV calcium gluconate 1 g (10 mL of 10%)
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Loss of reflexes occurs at ~7 mmol/L, respiratory depression at higher levels; monitor reflexes, RR and urine output (>30 mL/h).

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A primigravida at 36 weeks has a generalised tonic–clonic seizure in the antenatal clinic. What is the drug of choice to control and prevent further seizures?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: MgSO₄ is superior to diazepam and phenytoin (Collaborative Eclampsia Trial); stabilise then deliver.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman at 32 weeks has painless, bright red vaginal bleeding. The uterus is soft and non-tender with a high presenting part. What should be AVOIDED until placental location is known?
o: Speculum examination by a senior doctor
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: VE may provoke massive haemorrhage in placenta praevia; confirm with transvaginal ultrasound (safe).

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A hypertensive woman at 35 weeks has sudden severe abdominal pain, dark vaginal bleeding, a tense "woody-hard" tender uterus and absent fetal heart sounds. Her BP is 90/60 mmHg. What is the most important complication to monitor?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Concealed abruption underestimates blood loss; with fetal death, vaginal delivery is usually preferred after correcting coagulopathy.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman with three previous caesarean sections has an anterior low-lying placenta at 28 weeks. What is she at high risk of?
o: Placenta accreta spectrum requiring planned caesarean hysterectomy at a specialised centre
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Risk of accreta increases with number of caesareans and placenta praevia; MRI/Doppler help diagnosis; plan delivery at 34–36 weeks.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: During amniotomy, sudden fresh vaginal bleeding occurs with fetal bradycardia while the mother remains stable. What is the diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Fetal blood loss causes rapid fetal exsanguination; emergency caesarean section.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: Immediately after vaginal delivery, a woman bleeds 800 mL. The uterus is boggy and above the umbilicus. After calling for help and uterine massage, which drug is first-line?
o: Oxytocin 10 IU IM/IV (or carbetocin) followed by oxytocin infusion
Ergometrine in a woman with pre-eclampsia
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Uterine atony is the commonest cause (Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin); tranexamic acid within 3 hours (WOMAN trial) is added.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: Which condition is a contraindication to carboprost (15-methyl PGF2α) in postpartum haemorrhage?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Carboprost causes bronchospasm; ergometrine is contraindicated in hypertension/pre-eclampsia.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: PPH continues despite uterotonics, bimanual compression and tranexamic acid. The uterus is atonic. Which is the next appropriate step before hysterectomy?
o: Intrauterine balloon tamponade (e.g., Bakri or condom catheter), then surgical measures such as B-Lynch suture
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Condom catheter tamponade is a low-cost option in Pakistan; other steps include uterine artery ligation, embolisation and hysterectomy.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: The placenta has not been delivered 60 minutes after vaginal birth despite active management; bleeding is minimal. What is the management?
o: Manual removal of placenta under anaesthesia with antibiotic cover
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Retained placenta: >30 min with active management (>60 min physiological); manual removal in theatre.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: During the third stage of labour with excessive cord traction, a woman suddenly develops shock out of proportion to blood loss and a mass protrudes from the vagina; the fundus is not palpable abdominally. What is the immediate management?
o: Remove the placenta first, then wait
Immediate manual replacement of the uterus (Johnson manoeuvre) with resuscitation
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Replace immediately (placenta left attached if not separated); tocolytics may help; oxytocin only after replacement.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman at 30 weeks has regular painful contractions with cervical dilatation of 2 cm and intact membranes. Which is the tocolytic of choice to allow steroids to act?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Tocolysis for 48 hours enables corticosteroids and in-utero transfer; atosiban is an alternative; MgSO₄ <32 weeks is given for fetal neuroprotection.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman at 31 weeks has a gush of clear fluid; speculum shows pooling of liquor. There are no contractions and no signs of infection. What is the management?
o: Oral erythromycin for 10 days, antenatal corticosteroids and monitoring for chorioamnionitis
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Co-amoxiclav increases NEC risk (ORACLE); avoid digital VE; delivery at ~37 weeks if uncomplicated.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman with PPROM at 33 weeks develops fever 38.5°C, maternal tachycardia, uterine tenderness and foul-smelling liquor. What is the management?
o: IV broad-spectrum antibiotics and expedite delivery
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Clinical chorioamnionitis requires delivery regardless of gestation to prevent maternal and neonatal sepsis.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: At 32 weeks, ultrasound shows estimated fetal weight <3rd centile. Umbilical artery Doppler shows absent end-diastolic flow. What does this indicate?
o: Significant placental insufficiency requiring close surveillance (daily CTG, ductus venosus Doppler) and planned delivery, with steroids
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Reversed end-diastolic flow or abnormal ductus venosus warrants delivery; MgSO₄ for neuroprotection if <32 weeks.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A healthy woman with an uncomplicated pregnancy is at 41 weeks. What is recommended to reduce perinatal mortality?
o: Elective caesarean at 41 weeks for all
Offer induction of labour between 41+0 and 42+0 weeks (after membrane sweep)
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Stillbirth risk rises after 41 weeks; if declining induction, offer increased monitoring (CTG and liquor volume).

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman scheduled for induction has a Bishop score of 3. What is the most appropriate initial method?
o: Cervical ripening with vaginal prostaglandin (dinoprostone) or misoprostol, or a balloon catheter
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Bishop score ≤6 = unfavourable cervix needing ripening; >8 favourable for amniotomy/oxytocin.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: On the WHO partograph, the cervicograph of a primigravida crosses the action line during active labour. What does this indicate?
o: Abnormal progress requiring senior assessment and intervention (e.g., augmentation or caesarean section)
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: The action line lies 4 hours to the right of the alert line (1 cm/hour); WHO Labour Care Guide (2020) uses time limits per cm instead.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: During labour, the CTG shows baseline 150 bpm, reduced variability (<5 bpm for 60 min) and recurrent late decelerations. What is the next step?
o: Classify as pathological; correct reversible causes and perform fetal blood sampling or expedite delivery
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Late decelerations indicate uteroplacental insufficiency; stop oxytocin, left lateral position, IV fluids, and consider delivery.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: Decelerations on CTG that mirror contractions, starting and ending with them, with a nadir at the contraction peak, are due to:
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Early decelerations are physiological; variable decelerations reflect cord compression; late decelerations reflect placental insufficiency.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: After delivery of the head, the "turtle sign" is noted and gentle traction fails to deliver the shoulders. What is the first manoeuvre after calling for help?
o: McRoberts manoeuvre (hyperflexion of maternal hips) with suprapubic pressure
Strong downward traction on the head
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: HELPERR mnemonic; fundal pressure worsens impaction; brachial plexus injury (Erb's palsy) is a common neonatal complication.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: After spontaneous rupture of membranes at 38 weeks, the umbilical cord is felt in the vagina with fetal bradycardia. The cervix is 5 cm dilated. What is the immediate management?
o: Push the cord back into the uterus forcefully
Elevate the presenting part (manually or bladder filling), knee–chest position, and category 1 caesarean section
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Avoid handling the cord to prevent vasospasm; instrumental delivery only if fully dilated and delivery imminent.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A healthy primigravida at 36 weeks has an uncomplicated breech presentation. What should be offered?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: ECV success ~50%; contraindications include placenta praevia, APH, ruptured membranes; Term Breech Trial favoured planned CS if ECV fails.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: Ultrasound at 12 weeks shows twins with a "T-sign" at the inter-twin membrane junction. What is the chorionicity and main risk?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Lambda (twin peak) sign = dichorionic; T-sign = monochorionic; MCDA twins need scans every 2 weeks from 16 weeks; laser ablation for TTTS.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman with one previous lower segment caesarean for fetal distress wants vaginal birth in this uncomplicated pregnancy. What is the approximate risk of uterine rupture in planned VBAC?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Success rate of VBAC is 72–75%; induction with prostaglandins increases rupture risk; contraindicated after classical caesarean.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman with a previous caesarean in augmented labour suddenly develops severe abdominal pain, cessation of contractions, fetal bradycardia, loss of station and maternal tachycardia. What is the diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Uterine rupture requires immediate laparotomy; scar tenderness and abnormal CTG are early signs.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A multigravida in prolonged labour in a rural area has a Bandl's retraction ring, fetal distress and haematuria. What is the long-term complication she is at risk of if she survives vaginal delivery after days of obstruction?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Prolonged pressure necrosis of the bladder/rectum; prevention through skilled birth attendance and timely caesarean section.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: After a forceps delivery, a perineal tear involves the external anal sphincter (<50% thickness) but not the internal sphincter. How is it classified?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: 3a <50% EAS; 3b >50% EAS; 3c includes IAS; 4th involves anal mucosa. Repair in theatre, antibiotics, laxatives, follow-up.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: Which is a prerequisite for a safe ventouse or forceps delivery?
o: Fully dilated cervix, ruptured membranes, head at or below ischial spines and no more than 1/5 palpable abdominally
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: FORCEPS mnemonic: Fully dilated, OA/OP position known, Ruptured membranes, Cephalic, Empty bladder, Pain relief, Station at or below spines.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman in labour has a fetal bradycardia of 70 bpm for 8 minutes. Which category of caesarean section applies?
o: Category 1 – immediate threat to life of woman or fetus (decision-to-delivery ~30 minutes)
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Category 2: compromise not immediately life-threatening (within 75 min); 3: needs early delivery; 4: planned.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman on day 4 after caesarean section has fever 39°C, tachycardia, foul-smelling lochia and a tender subinvoluted uterus. What is the most likely diagnosis and treatment?
o: Endometritis; IV broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., clindamycin plus gentamicin) after cultures
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Group A Streptococcus can cause rapidly fatal sepsis; use Sepsis Six; exclude retained products by ultrasound.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman 7 days after delivery has insomnia, confusion, hallucinations and believes her baby is possessed. She has a history of bipolar disorder. What is the management?
o: Start an SSRI and review in 6 weeks
Urgent psychiatric admission (mother and baby unit) as a psychiatric emergency
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Postpartum psychosis risks suicide and infanticide; bipolar disorder is the strongest risk factor.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A breastfeeding woman at 6 weeks postpartum wants hormonal contraception. Which method is most suitable according to WHO MEC?
o: Combined oral contraceptive pill at 3 weeks
No contraception needed until periods return beyond 6 months in all women
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Combined methods are MEC 4 before 6 weeks in breastfeeding women; LAM is effective only if exclusively breastfeeding, amenorrhoeic and <6 months.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman with Graves disease becomes pregnant (6 weeks). Which antithyroid drug is preferred in the first trimester?
o: Propylthiouracil, switching to carbimazole/methimazole in the second trimester
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Carbimazole causes embryopathy (aplasia cutis) in the first trimester; PTU causes hepatotoxicity so is limited to the first trimester.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: Which antiepileptic drug carries the highest risk of congenital malformations and neurodevelopmental delay and should be avoided in women of childbearing potential?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Valproate: ~10% malformation risk (neural tube defects) and ~30–40% neurodevelopmental disorders; lamotrigine and levetiracetam are safer.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A pregnant woman with rheumatic mitral stenosis develops pulmonary oedema at 28 weeks. Why does she decompensate at this stage?
o: Increased cardiac output, blood volume and heart rate shorten diastolic filling across the stenotic valve
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Blood volume rises ~40–50%, peaking at 28–32 weeks; beta-blockers, diuretics, and balloon valvotomy if refractory.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A mother is HBsAg and HBeAg positive with high viral load. What should the newborn receive?
o: Hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis B immunoglobulin within 12 hours of birth
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Maternal tenofovir from 28 weeks if viral load >200,000 IU/mL; breastfeeding is not contraindicated.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A pregnant woman is newly diagnosed with HIV at 20 weeks. What is the most effective intervention to prevent mother-to-child transmission?
o: Start lifelong ART immediately (e.g., TLD) to achieve undetectable viral load, with infant prophylaxis
Wait until delivery to start ART
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: With viral suppression, transmission risk falls below 1%; mode of delivery depends on viral load at 36 weeks.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman in labour at term had GBS bacteriuria earlier in this pregnancy. What is recommended?
o: Intrapartum IV benzylpenicillin from onset of labour
Treat the baby with antibiotics for 7 days routinely
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Intrapartum prophylaxis reduces early-onset neonatal GBS sepsis; clindamycin if penicillin allergic.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman at 33 weeks has intense itching of palms and soles, worse at night, without rash. Serum bile acids are 45 µmol/L with mildly raised ALT. What is the diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Stillbirth risk rises significantly with bile acids ≥100 µmol/L; ursodeoxycholic acid relieves itch; resolves after delivery.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A primigravida at 36 weeks has nausea, abdominal pain, jaundice, hypoglycaemia, raised ammonia, prolonged PT and AKI. What is the management?
o: Stabilise (glucose, correct coagulopathy) and deliver promptly
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: AFLP (associated with fetal LCHAD deficiency) is a medical emergency; hypoglycaemia helps distinguish it from HELLP.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: During labour, a woman suddenly develops breathlessness, cyanosis, hypotension, seizures and then massive bleeding from DIC. What is the likely diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: AFE is a clinical diagnosis of exclusion; management is supportive (ALS, perimortem caesarean within 4–5 min of arrest, massive transfusion).

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman at 30 weeks has a swollen, painful left calf. Compression ultrasound confirms DVT. What is the treatment?
o: Therapeutic LMWH (weight-based) for the rest of pregnancy and at least 6 weeks postpartum (total ≥3 months)
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Warfarin is teratogenic and DOACs are not recommended; both warfarin and LMWH are compatible with breastfeeding.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: Ultrasound at 30 weeks shows amniotic fluid index 30 cm. Which fetal condition should be looked for?
o: Oesophageal atresia or other upper GI obstruction
Fetal growth restriction with placental insufficiency
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Polyhydramnios: maternal diabetes, fetal swallowing problems (GI atresia, neuromuscular), twin-twin transfusion; oligohydramnios: renal agenesis, PUV, FGR, ROM.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: After a massive PPH with prolonged hypotension, a woman fails to lactate and later develops amenorrhoea, fatigue and hypothyroid features. What is the diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: The enlarged pituitary of pregnancy is vulnerable to ischaemia; replace cortisol before thyroxine.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman with two previous painless second-trimester losses at 18–20 weeks with cervical dilatation has come for pre-pregnancy advice. What is recommended in the next pregnancy?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Ultrasound-indicated cerclage (cervix <25 mm before 24 weeks with previous preterm birth) or vaginal progesterone are other strategies.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: According to the WHO definition, maternal death is the death of a woman while pregnant or within how many days of termination of pregnancy from causes related to or aggravated by pregnancy?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Leading causes of maternal death in Pakistan include PPH, hypertensive disorders, sepsis, obstructed labour and unsafe abortion.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: What is the recommended timing of cord clamping in a healthy term baby not requiring resuscitation?
o: After delivery of the placenta only
Only after the baby cries for 5 minutes
Not earlier than 1 minute after birth (1–3 minutes)
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Delayed clamping improves iron stores in infancy and reduces transfusion and IVH in preterms.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A pregnant woman at 12 weeks has >10⁵ CFU/mL E. coli on routine urine culture without symptoms. What is the management?
o: Treat with an antibiotic guided by sensitivity (e.g., nitrofurantoin or cephalexin) and repeat culture
No treatment as she is asymptomatic
Trimethoprim in the first trimester as first choice
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Untreated bacteriuria in pregnancy leads to pyelonephritis and preterm birth; trimethoprim (folate antagonist) is avoided in the first trimester.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A pregnant woman at 10 weeks is exposed to a child with rubella. Her rubella IgG is negative and IgM becomes positive 3 weeks later. What is the major fetal risk?
o: Congenital rubella syndrome with high risk (up to ~90%) of defects
No fetal risk in the first trimester
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: Risk is highest before 12 weeks (cataracts, deafness, PDA); MMR vaccine is contraindicated in pregnancy and should be given postpartum.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.s: A woman on lisinopril for hypertension discovers she is 7 weeks pregnant. What is the appropriate action?
o: Stop lisinopril and switch to labetalol, nifedipine or methyldopa
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/obstetric.e: ACEi/ARBs cause fetal renal dysgenesis, oligohydramnios and skull defects, particularly in second/third trimesters.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 24-year-old woman has oligomenorrhoea, acne and hirsutism. Ultrasound shows 22 follicles in each ovary. According to the Rotterdam criteria, how many features are required for diagnosis?
o: Two of three: oligo/anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovarian morphology (after excluding other causes)
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Exclude thyroid disease, hyperprolactinaemia and non-classic CAH (17-OHP); AMH may replace ultrasound in adults (2023 guideline).

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A woman with PCOS (BMI 29) wants to conceive; her partner's semen analysis and her tubal patency are normal. After lifestyle modification, what is first-line ovulation induction?
o: Metformin alone as the only option
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Letrozole gives higher live birth rates than clomiphene in PCOS; gonadotrophins or ovarian drilling are second-line.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A woman with PCOS has had only 2 periods per year for several years. Which long-term risk requires protection?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Unopposed oestrogen; induce withdrawal bleeds at least every 3–4 months with progestogens or use COCP/LNG-IUS; also screen for diabetes and dyslipidaemia.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 16-year-old girl has primary amenorrhoea with normal breast and pubic hair development, cyclical pelvic pain and a bluish bulging membrane at the introitus. What is the diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Treated by hymenotomy (cruciate incision); transverse vaginal septum presents similarly without bulging hymen.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 17-year-old with primary amenorrhoea has normal secondary sexual characteristics, normal pubic hair, a short blind vagina and absent uterus on ultrasound. Karyotype is 46,XX. What is the diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Ovaries function normally; associated renal anomalies; vaginal dilators or vaginoplasty; surrogacy for fertility.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 16-year-old with short stature, absent breast development and primary amenorrhoea has FSH 90 IU/L. What is the most likely karyotype?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Hypergonadotrophic hypogonadism due to streak gonads; oestrogen replacement for puberty and bone health; growth hormone for height.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 17-year-old girl with primary amenorrhoea, absent secondary sexual development and anosmia has low FSH and LH. What is the diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Failure of GnRH neuron migration with olfactory bulb hypoplasia; pulsatile GnRH or gonadotrophins induce fertility.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 26-year-old woman has had no periods for 4 months. What is the FIRST investigation?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Pregnancy is the commonest cause; then TSH, prolactin, FSH/LH, testosterone.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A woman develops secondary amenorrhoea after repeated dilatation and curettage for retained products following a postpartum haemorrhage. Hormone levels are normal and progesterone challenge produces no bleed. What is the diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Diagnosed and treated by hysteroscopic adhesiolysis; causes infertility and recurrent miscarriage.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 34-year-old woman has amenorrhoea for 6 months with hot flushes. FSH is 60 IU/L on two occasions 4 weeks apart. What is the recommended management?
o: Hormone replacement therapy (or COCP) until at least the average age of menopause
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: POI (<40 years) increases osteoporosis and cardiovascular risk; screen karyotype, FMR1 premutation and autoimmune disease.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 52-year-old woman with a uterus has troublesome vasomotor symptoms. Which HRT is appropriate?
o: Combined oestrogen plus progestogen (e.g., transdermal oestradiol with micronised progesterone)
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Women with a uterus need a progestogen for endometrial protection; transdermal oestrogen has no increased VTE risk.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: Which condition is a contraindication to systemic HRT?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Other contraindications: undiagnosed vaginal bleeding, active liver disease, active/recent arterial thromboembolism, untreated endometrial hyperplasia.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 60-year-old obese diabetic woman has vaginal bleeding 8 years after menopause. Transvaginal ultrasound shows endometrial thickness of 9 mm. What is the next step?
o: Endometrial biopsy (pipelle) or hysteroscopy with biopsy
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Endometrial thickness ≥4 mm in postmenopausal bleeding requires histology to exclude endometrial carcinoma.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: Which factor is PROTECTIVE against endometrial carcinoma?
o: Use of the combined oral contraceptive pill
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Other risk factors: late menopause, PCOS, unopposed oestrogen, diabetes. Smoking and COCP are associated with lower risk.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 48-year-old woman's endometrial biopsy shows atypical endometrial hyperplasia (endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia). She has completed her family. What is recommended?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Atypical hyperplasia carries high risk of coexisting/progression to carcinoma; LNG-IUS with close surveillance if fertility desired.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: According to FIGO PALM-COEIN classification, which of the following is a STRUCTURAL cause of abnormal uterine bleeding?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: PALM (structural): Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, Malignancy/hyperplasia; COEIN (non-structural): Coagulopathy, Ovulatory, Endometrial, Iatrogenic, Not classified.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 38-year-old woman has heavy regular periods with no structural abnormality on ultrasound. She wants contraception. What is first-line treatment?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: LNG-IUS is most effective medical therapy; tranexamic acid/NSAIDs if contraception not wanted.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 35-year-old nulliparous woman has menorrhagia and infertility. Ultrasound shows a 3 cm submucosal fibroid (FIGO type 0). What is the treatment of choice?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Submucosal fibroids distort the cavity and cause bleeding/infertility; hysteroscopic resection preserves fertility.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A woman at 20 weeks of pregnancy with a known fibroid has acute localised abdominal pain, low-grade fever and tenderness over the fibroid. What is the management?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Red (carneous) degeneration occurs in pregnancy due to haemorrhagic infarction; NSAIDs are avoided in later pregnancy.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 29-year-old woman has progressive dysmenorrhoea, deep dyspareunia, dyschezia and infertility. Examination shows a fixed retroverted uterus with uterosacral nodularity. What is the gold standard for diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Transvaginal ultrasound/MRI can identify endometriomas and deep disease; laparoscopy allows diagnosis and treatment.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 44-year-old multiparous woman has heavy painful periods and a uniformly enlarged, boggy, tender uterus of 12 weeks size. What is the likely diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: MRI shows thickened junctional zone; hysterectomy is definitive; LNG-IUS for symptom control.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: According to WHO recommendations, what is the preferred primary cervical cancer screening test?
o: HPV DNA testing, starting at age 30 and repeated every 5–10 years
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: WHO's 90-70-90 strategy for cervical cancer elimination: HPV vaccination, screening with high-performance test, treatment of precancer.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: Which HPV types are the main causes of cervical cancer targeted by vaccines?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: HPV 16/18 cause ~70% of cervical cancers; 6/11 cause genital warts. WHO recommends a single-dose schedule for girls 9–14; Pakistan launched HPV vaccination in 2025.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: Colposcopy-directed biopsy in a 32-year-old shows CIN 3. What is the treatment?
o: Large loop excision of the transformation zone (LLETZ)
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Excisional treatment; follow-up HPV test of cure at 6 months.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 45-year-old woman has a cervical carcinoma extending to the lower third of the vagina without pelvic side wall involvement or hydronephrosis. What is the FIGO stage?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: IIIA: lower third of vagina; IIIB: pelvic wall or hydronephrosis; IIIC: lymph nodes; IVA: bladder/rectal mucosa. Stage IB3–IVA: chemoradiation.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 35-year-old woman has postcoital bleeding for 3 months. Speculum examination shows a friable irregular growth on the cervix. What is the next step?
o: Urgent colposcopy and biopsy of the lesion
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: A visible cervical lesion requires biopsy regardless of prior normal smear results.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 22-year-old woman has sudden-onset severe unilateral pelvic pain with nausea and vomiting. Ultrasound shows a 7 cm ovarian cyst with reduced Doppler flow. What is the management?
o: Urgent laparoscopy with detorsion (and cystectomy), preserving the ovary
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Doppler flow may be present despite torsion; ovary often recovers after detorsion even if dusky.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 25-year-old woman has a pelvic mass; ultrasound shows an ovarian cyst with echogenic fat, hair and a calcified tooth-like structure. What is the diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Commonest ovarian neoplasm in young women; risk of torsion; managed with ovarian cystectomy.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 58-year-old postmenopausal woman has a complex multiloculated ovarian mass with solid areas and ascites. CA-125 is 450 U/mL. What is the next step?
o: Laparoscopic cystectomy in a general unit
Refer to a gynaecological oncology centre for staging CT and cytoreductive surgery
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: RMI = U × M × CA-125 (here >200 = high risk); epithelial ovarian cancer is managed by optimal debulking and platinum chemotherapy.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A postmenopausal woman has a solid ovarian mass, ascites and right pleural effusion that resolve completely after removal of the tumour. What is the tumour?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Meigs syndrome is benign; effusions resolve after excision.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 60-year-old woman with postmenopausal bleeding has endometrial hyperplasia and an ovarian mass. Histology shows Call–Exner bodies. Which marker is useful for follow-up?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Granulosa cell tumours produce oestrogen (endometrial hyperplasia/cancer); inhibin B and AMH are tumour markers.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 19-year-old woman has a rapidly growing solid ovarian mass with markedly raised serum LDH; AFP and hCG are normal. What is the likely tumour?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Dysgerminoma (ovarian counterpart of seminoma): LDH; yolk sac: AFP; choriocarcinoma: hCG. Highly chemosensitive; fertility-sparing surgery.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A couple has failed to conceive after 1 year of regular unprotected intercourse. What is the first investigation for the male partner?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: WHO 2021 lower reference limits: volume 1.4 mL, concentration 16 million/mL, total motility 42%, normal forms 4%.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A woman with 28-day cycles is being investigated for infertility. When should serum progesterone be measured to confirm ovulation?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Mid-luteal progesterone >30 nmol/L confirms ovulation; for a 35-day cycle, test on day 28.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A woman with no history of PID, endometriosis or ectopic pregnancy needs tubal assessment for infertility. What is the recommended test?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Laparoscopy and dye test is preferred when comorbidities (PID, endometriosis) are suspected.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: Five days after hCG trigger in IVF, a woman has abdominal distension, nausea, oliguria, ascites, haematocrit 48% and enlarged ovaries. What is the diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Increased vascular permeability (VEGF) causes third-space fluid loss, haemoconcentration and thrombosis; supportive care, thromboprophylaxis, paracentesis.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: Which woman has an absolute contraindication (UKMEC 4) to the combined oral contraceptive pill?
o: A 32-year-old with family history of ovarian cancer
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: UKMEC 4 also includes smoker ≥35 years (≥15/day), history of VTE, known thrombogenic mutation, BP ≥160/100, current breast cancer, <6 weeks postpartum breastfeeding.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A woman had unprotected intercourse 4 days (96 hours) ago. What is the MOST effective method of emergency contraception?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Copper IUD is effective up to 5 days after intercourse (or ovulation); ulipristal up to 120 h; levonorgestrel up to 72 h.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A woman on COCP forgot to take two pills in the first week of a new pack and had unprotected sex 2 days ago. What advice is correct?
o: Stop the pack and start a new pack in 1 week
Take all missed pills together and no further precautions
Take the most recent missed pill now, continue the pack, use condoms for 7 days, and consider emergency contraception
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Missing ≥2 pills in week 1 with intercourse in the pill-free interval or week 1 requires EC consideration.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 17-year-old wants long-term injectable contraception with depot medroxyprogesterone acetate. Which adverse effect is specific to this method?
o: Increased VTE risk higher than COCP
Increased menstrual blood loss in most users
Reduction in bone mineral density (reversible) and delayed return to fertility
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: DMPA fertility return may take up to 1 year; weight gain is common; consider alternatives in adolescents.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 23-year-old woman has lower abdominal pain, fever, deep dyspareunia, cervical motion tenderness and mucopurulent discharge. She is haemodynamically stable. What is the outpatient treatment?
o: IM ceftriaxone 1 g single dose plus oral doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Complications: tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain, Fitz-Hugh–Curtis syndrome (perihepatitis); treat partners.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A woman has thin, greyish-white homogeneous discharge with a fishy odour, pH 5.5 and positive whiff test. Microscopy shows clue cells. What is the treatment?
o: Oral metronidazole 400–500 mg twice daily for 5–7 days
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Amsel's criteria; BV in pregnancy is associated with preterm birth; partner treatment is not required.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A woman has frothy yellow-green offensive vaginal discharge, vulval itch and a "strawberry cervix". What is the treatment?
o: Metronidazole for her and her sexual partner(s)
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Trichomonas vaginalis is sexually transmitted; motile flagellated protozoa seen on wet mount or NAAT.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 65-year-old multiparous woman with a vaginal "lump" has a uterine prolapse to the introitus. She is frail with significant cardiorespiratory disease. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Vaginal ring pessary with pelvic floor exercises and topical oestrogen
Vaginal hysterectomy with repair under GA
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Pessaries suit women unfit for surgery or who prefer to avoid it; change every 6 months.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 50-year-old multiparous woman leaks urine when coughing, sneezing and lifting, without urgency. What is first-line management?
o: Supervised pelvic floor muscle training for at least 3 months
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Stress incontinence: pelvic floor exercises, then surgery (colposuspension, autologous sling); urge incontinence: bladder training, antimuscarinics/mirabegron.

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A woman from a remote area had a prolonged obstructed labour at home 6 weeks ago with stillbirth. She now has continuous dribbling of urine per vagina. What is the most likely diagnosis?
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Diagnosed by the three-swab (dye) test; surgical repair at a fistula centre after tissue inflammation settles (or early for small fistulas with catheter drainage).

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 30-year-old woman has a painful, tense, fluctuant swelling in the posterior part of the left labium majus. What is the treatment?
o: Simple incision without drainage in all
Excision of the gland as first line
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Marsupialisation reduces recurrence; excision is reserved for recurrent cases or postmenopausal women (exclude carcinoma).

endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.s: A 62-year-old woman has vulval itching and white, atrophic, crinkled "figure of eight" plaques around the vulva and anus with loss of labia minora. What is the treatment and long-term risk?
o: Ultrapotent topical steroid (clobetasol); risk of vulval squamous cell carcinoma
endocrine-and-reproduction-iii/gynaecolo.e: Lifelong follow-up; biopsy any non-healing ulcer or thickened area.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 62-year-old man developed right hemiparesis and aphasia 2 hours ago. CT brain shows no haemorrhage; BP 165/95 mmHg, glucose 140 mg/dL, INR 1.0. What is the most appropriate treatment?
o: IV thrombolysis with alteplase (or tenecteplase) as soon as possible
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Thrombolysis is indicated within 4.5 hours of onset after excluding haemorrhage and contraindications; aspirin is started 24 hours later.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A patient presents 5 hours after stroke onset with NIHSS 18. CT angiography shows a proximal middle cerebral artery (M1) occlusion with a small infarct core. What is the best treatment?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Thrombectomy benefits large vessel occlusion up to 6 hours, and up to 24 hours with favourable perfusion imaging (DAWN/DEFUSE-3).

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A patient with acute ischaemic stroke who is NOT a candidate for thrombolysis has BP 200/110 mmHg. What is the appropriate management?
o: Permissive hypertension; treat only if BP >220/120 mmHg or there is another indication
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Lowering BP reduces penumbral perfusion; for thrombolysis candidates, BP must be <185/110 mmHg.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 68-year-old had a 20-minute episode of right arm weakness and slurred speech yesterday, now fully resolved. What is the immediate management?
o: Aspirin plus clopidogrel (short-course dual therapy), urgent carotid imaging and specialist assessment within 24 hours
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Highest stroke risk is in the first 48 hours; 21-day DAPT then single antiplatelet (CHANCE/POINT); assess for AF and carotid stenosis.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A patient with a recent TIA in the left carotid territory has 80% stenosis of the left internal carotid artery. What is recommended?
o: Bilateral carotid stenting regardless of side
Carotid endarterectomy within 2 weeks along with best medical therapy
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Symptomatic stenosis 50–99% benefits from early endarterectomy; benefit falls with delay.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A hypertensive diabetic develops pure motor hemiparesis affecting face, arm and leg equally, without sensory loss, visual field defect or aphasia. Where is the lesion most likely?
o: Brainstem pons with cranial nerve palsy
Posterior limb of the internal capsule (lacunar infarct)
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Lacunar syndromes arise from small perforating artery disease; classic syndromes include pure motor, pure sensory, ataxic hemiparesis and dysarthria–clumsy hand.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A patient has sudden vertigo, ipsilateral facial numbness, Horner syndrome, hoarseness, dysphagia and contralateral loss of pain and temperature in the body. Which artery is occluded?
o: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery (lateral medullary/Wallenberg syndrome)
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Wallenberg syndrome: crossed sensory loss, ataxia, nystagmus, dysphagia; high aspiration risk.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A patient with atrial fibrillation has a moderate ischaemic stroke. When should oral anticoagulation be started?
o: Only if there is a second stroke
After a delay based on infarct size and haemorrhage risk (commonly 5–14 days; earlier for TIA/small strokes)
Immediately with IV heparin in all patients
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Early DOAC initiation is increasingly supported for small/moderate infarcts (e.g., ELAN trial); large infarcts need longer delay.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A hypertensive patient has sudden headache, vomiting and left hemiplegia. CT shows a right basal ganglia haemorrhage with BP 210/115 mmHg. What is the appropriate BP management?
o: Lower systolic BP towards 140 mmHg (avoiding a drop below ~130) using IV antihypertensives
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: INTERACT/ATACH: intensive but smooth BP lowering; reverse anticoagulation; neurosurgical referral for cerebellar haemorrhage or hydrocephalus.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 45-year-old woman has a sudden "worst ever" occipital headache with neck stiffness and photophobia. CT brain 8 hours later is normal. What is the next step?
o: Lumbar puncture after 12 hours from onset looking for xanthochromia
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: CT sensitivity falls after 6 hours; xanthochromia (bilirubin) confirms SAH; then CT angiography and coiling/clipping. Nimodipine prevents delayed cerebral ischaemia.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 28-year-old woman on the combined pill has 5 days of worsening headache, papilloedema and a seizure. CT shows a haemorrhagic infarct not confined to an arterial territory. What is the treatment?
o: Anticoagulation with heparin followed by oral anticoagulant, even with haemorrhagic infarction
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: CVST is confirmed by MR/CT venography ("empty delta sign"); anticoagulation is standard despite haemorrhage.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A patient has been convulsing for 6 minutes. IV access is available. What is the first-line drug?
o: IV lorazepam 4 mg (or IV diazepam/IM midazolam if no access)
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: After two doses of benzodiazepine, give a second-line agent (levetiracetam, phenytoin or valproate); then anaesthesia with intubation.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 25-year-old has a first generalised tonic–clonic seizure. Examination, CT and EEG are normal and there are no provoking factors. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Counselling about driving and safety, with antiepileptic drugs generally deferred unless risk factors for recurrence
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Treatment is usually started after a second seizure, or after the first if EEG/MRI abnormality or high recurrence risk.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: Which is the preferred first-line drug for focal epilepsy?
o: Sodium valproate for women of childbearing age
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Focal: lamotrigine/levetiracetam; generalised tonic–clonic: valproate (males) or lamotrigine/levetiracetam; absence: ethosuximide; myoclonic: levetiracetam.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A patient on long-term phenytoin has gum hypertrophy, ataxia and coarse facial features. Which additional risk is associated with chronic use?
o: Haemolytic anaemia due to G6PD inhibition
Osteomalacia due to vitamin D metabolism induction and folate deficiency
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Phenytoin has zero-order kinetics; toxicity causes nystagmus, ataxia and dysarthria.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 28-year-old woman has a moderate–severe unilateral throbbing headache with nausea and photophobia. Which is an appropriate acute treatment?
o: Prophylactic propranolol taken during attacks only
Oral sumatriptan with an NSAID and an antiemetic
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Avoid triptans in uncontrolled hypertension or ischaemic heart disease; limit acute drugs to <10–15 days/month to avoid medication-overuse headache.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A woman has 8 migraine days per month affecting work. She has asthma. Which prophylactic drug is most appropriate?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Beta-blockers are avoided in asthma; topiramate is teratogenic so needs contraception counselling; CGRP monoclonals are newer options.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 35-year-old man has severe unilateral periorbital pain lasting 45 minutes, occurring nightly for 3 weeks, with ipsilateral lacrimation, conjunctival injection and nasal congestion. What is the acute treatment?
o: High-flow oxygen 100% by non-rebreather mask plus subcutaneous sumatriptan
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Verapamil is used for prophylaxis; patients are typically restless (unlike migraine).

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: An obese 25-year-old woman has headaches, transient visual obscurations and bilateral papilloedema. Imaging is normal; CSF opening pressure is 32 cmH₂O with normal constituents. What is the first-line drug treatment?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Monitor visual fields; optic nerve sheath fenestration or CSF shunting if vision deteriorates; stop precipitating drugs (tetracyclines, vitamin A, OCP).

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 20-year-old has fever, neck stiffness, photophobia and a purpuric rash. He is drowsy but has no focal signs. What is the correct order of management?
o: Lumbar puncture first in all patients before antibiotics
Blood cultures and immediate IV ceftriaxone (plus dexamethasone), then lumbar puncture if no contraindication
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Do not delay antibiotics; CT before LP if reduced GCS, focal signs, seizures or immunocompromise; notify public health and give contact prophylaxis.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: CSF shows: appearance turbid, WBC 2,500/µL (90% neutrophils), protein 200 mg/dL, glucose 20 mg/dL (blood glucose 100 mg/dL). What is the diagnosis?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Bacterial: neutrophils, high protein, very low glucose. TB/fungal: lymphocytes, very high protein, low glucose. Viral: lymphocytes, normal glucose.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old has 3 weeks of headache, fever, vomiting and confusion with a sixth nerve palsy. CSF shows lymphocytosis, protein 250 mg/dL and low glucose. What treatment should be added to anti-TB drugs?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Steroids reduce mortality in TB meningitis; treatment is 12 months; hydrocephalus and basal exudates are typical (common in Pakistan).

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 40-year-old has fever, confusion, personality change and temporal lobe seizures. MRI shows temporal lobe hyperintensity and CSF shows lymphocytes with red cells. What is the treatment?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Delay increases mortality; confirm with CSF HSV PCR but treat empirically on suspicion.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: An HIV patient with CD4 40 cells/mm³ has 2 weeks of headache. CSF India ink shows encapsulated yeasts and opening pressure is 35 cmH₂O. Besides antifungals, what is essential?
o: Therapeutic lumbar punctures to control raised intracranial pressure
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Induction with amphotericin B plus flucytosine; steroids increase harm; delay ART by 4–6 weeks to avoid IRIS.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 25-year-old man from rural Punjab has a first seizure. CT shows a single ring-enhancing lesion with a central dot and perilesional oedema. What is the management?
o: Antiepileptic drug plus albendazole with corticosteroid cover
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Neurocysticercosis is the commonest cause of adult-onset seizures in endemic areas; "dot in a hole" sign is the scolex.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 28-year-old woman had optic neuritis last year and now has numbness and weakness of both legs for 1 week. MRI shows periventricular and spinal cord lesions, some enhancing. What supports the diagnosis?
o: Dissemination in time and space with oligoclonal bands in CSF
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: McDonald criteria; treat acute relapses with high-dose methylprednisolone; disease-modifying therapy reduces relapses.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A woman has severe bilateral optic neuritis and a longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis over 4 vertebral segments. Which antibody should be tested?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: NMOSD is treated differently from MS (rituximab, eculizumab); some MS drugs worsen it.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old man develops ascending symmetrical weakness with areflexia 2 weeks after diarrhoea. Which bedside measurement is most important for monitoring?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: FVC <20 mL/kg (or <1 L) or a falling trend indicates need for ventilation; SpO₂ falls late. Treat with IVIG or plasma exchange; steroids are ineffective.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old woman has fatigable ptosis, diplopia and proximal weakness worse in the evening. Which antibody is most commonly positive?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: CT chest for thymoma; treat with pyridostigmine plus immunosuppression; avoid aminoglycosides, quinolones and magnesium.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A patient with myasthenia gravis develops respiratory failure after an infection. What is the treatment?
o: Intubation/ventilatory support with IVIG or plasma exchange
Oral prednisolone alone started at high dose without monitoring
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Distinguish from cholinergic crisis (excess muscarinic effects); high-dose steroids alone can worsen weakness transiently.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 60-year-old smoker has proximal weakness that improves briefly with exercise, dry mouth and absent reflexes. What is the underlying association?
o: Small cell lung carcinoma with anti-voltage-gated calcium channel antibodies
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Post-exercise facilitation is characteristic; EMG shows incremental response at high-frequency stimulation.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 58-year-old has progressive asymmetric limb weakness with wasting, fasciculations, brisk reflexes and no sensory loss. What is the most likely diagnosis?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs without sensory involvement; riluzole prolongs survival modestly; NIV improves quality of life.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A diabetic patient has burning pain in both feet with stocking distribution sensory loss. Which drug is first-line for the neuropathic pain?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Glycaemic control prevents progression; foot care education prevents ulceration.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A patient has paraesthesia, loss of vibration and joint position sense, brisk knee jerks with absent ankle jerks and extensor plantars. What is the diagnosis?
o: Subacute combined degeneration of the cord due to vitamin B12 deficiency
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Dorsal columns and corticospinal tracts are affected; treat promptly with parenteral B12 (irreversible if delayed).

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old woman has sudden right facial weakness involving the forehead, with inability to close the right eye and loss of taste on the anterior tongue. What is the treatment?
o: Oral prednisolone within 72 hours plus eye protection (lubricants, taping at night)
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Forehead involvement indicates a lower motor neuron lesion; stroke spares the forehead. Antivirals may be added in severe cases (Ramsay Hunt needs aciclovir).

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 60-year-old has brief, severe electric-shock-like pains in the right cheek triggered by chewing and cold wind. What is the drug of choice?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: MRI to exclude secondary causes (MS, tumour, vascular loop); microvascular decompression for refractory cases.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 68-year-old man has resting tremor, bradykinesia, rigidity and a shuffling gait with reduced arm swing, responding to levodopa. Which pathology underlies this?
o: Loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra with Lewy bodies
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Levodopa with carbidopa is most effective; long-term motor fluctuations and dyskinesias develop.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 70-year-old on metoclopramide for nausea develops symmetrical bradykinesia and rigidity with minimal tremor. What is the management?
o: Stop the offending drug and observe for gradual improvement
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Dopamine antagonists (metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, typical antipsychotics) cause symmetrical parkinsonism; domperidone is a safer antiemetic.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 70-year-old has early falls (backwards), vertical gaze palsy, axial rigidity and poor levodopa response. What is the diagnosis?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: "Parkinson-plus" syndromes: PSP (gaze palsy, falls), MSA (autonomic failure, cerebellar), CBD (alien limb, apraxia).

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 55-year-old man has a bilateral action tremor of the hands, worse holding a cup, improving with alcohol, with a family history. What is the first-line treatment?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Essential tremor is postural/kinetic and symmetrical; Parkinson tremor is at rest and asymmetrical.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 40-year-old with a family history has chorea, personality change and cognitive decline. What is the genetic basis?
o: CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion in HTT on chromosome 4 (autosomal dominant with anticipation)
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Caudate atrophy with "boxcar" ventricles; genetic counselling is essential before predictive testing.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 22-year-old with tremor, dysarthria, dystonia and deranged LFTs has Kayser–Fleischer rings. Which investigation is most consistent with the diagnosis?
o: Low serum caeruloplasmin with raised 24-hour urinary copper
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Treat with chelation (penicillamine, trientine) or zinc; screen siblings; untreated disease is fatal.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 75-year-old has 2 years of progressive memory loss for recent events, word-finding difficulty and getting lost, with intact alertness. What is the first-line drug?
o: Memantine as first-line in mild disease
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Memantine is used in moderate–severe disease or intolerance; exclude reversible causes (B12, thyroid, depression, NPH).

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 72-year-old has fluctuating cognition, detailed visual hallucinations, parkinsonism and REM sleep behaviour disorder. Which drug class must be avoided?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Neuroleptic sensitivity can cause severe rigidity and death; rivastigmine helps cognition and hallucinations.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: An elderly man has gait apraxia ("magnetic gait"), urinary incontinence and cognitive slowing. CT shows ventriculomegaly out of proportion to atrophy. What is the treatment?
o: Ventriculoperitoneal shunt after a positive high-volume lumbar tap test
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Hakim's triad: "wet, wobbly and wacky"; gait improves most after shunting.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 60-year-old with prostate cancer has back pain, bilateral leg weakness, a sensory level at T10 and urinary retention. What is the immediate management?
o: Urgent MRI whole spine and high-dose dexamethasone, with radiotherapy or surgery
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Metastatic cord compression is an emergency; treatment within 24 hours preserves ambulation.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: After a stab wound to the back, a patient has right leg weakness with loss of vibration and proprioception, and left-sided loss of pain and temperature below the level. What is the lesion?
o: Right-sided hemisection of the spinal cord
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Ipsilateral corticospinal and dorsal column loss with contralateral spinothalamic loss (starting 1–2 segments below).

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 30-year-old has painless burns on the hands, loss of pain and temperature sensation over the shoulders and arms with preserved light touch, and wasting of small hand muscles. What is the diagnosis?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: "Cape-like" dissociated sensory loss from central cord cavitation; MRI confirms; often associated with Chiari I malformation.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 50-year-old has brief episodes of vertigo lasting under a minute when turning in bed. Dix–Hallpike test provokes rotatory nystagmus with latency and fatigue. What is the treatment?
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: BPPV is due to otoconia in the posterior semicircular canal; vestibular sedatives should be limited.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A 45-year-old has recurrent attacks of vertigo lasting hours with fluctuating low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus and aural fullness. What is the initial management?
o: Salt restriction with betahistine/diuretic, and vestibular sedatives for acute attacks
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Ménière disease reflects endolymphatic hydrops; intratympanic steroids or gentamicin for refractory cases.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A farmer develops trismus, risus sardonicus and painful generalised spasms 8 days after a penetrating foot injury. What is the treatment?
o: Human tetanus immunoglobulin, metronidazole, wound debridement, benzodiazepines and nursing in a quiet dark room
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Autonomic instability is common; active immunisation is required after recovery as disease does not confer immunity.

neurosciences-iii/medicine.s: A man is bitten on the hand by a stray dog that ran away. He has never been vaccinated. What is the correct post-exposure prophylaxis?
o: Thorough wound washing with soap and water, rabies immunoglobulin infiltrated around the wound, and a full course of rabies vaccine
Observation of the patient for 10 days
neurosciences-iii/medicine.e: Category III exposure requires RIG plus vaccine; rabies is almost always fatal once symptomatic.

neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.s: A 35-year-old has 8 weeks of low mood, anhedonia, insomnia with early morning waking, poor appetite, weight loss and feelings of worthlessness. What is the first-line pharmacological treatment?
o: Amitriptyline as first line in all
An SSRI (e.g., sertraline or fluoxetine) with psychological therapy
neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.e: Assess suicide risk; continue antidepressants for at least 6 months after remission; response takes 2–4 weeks.

neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.s: Which factor most increases short-term suicide risk in a depressed patient?
o: A specific plan with access to means and a previous attempt
neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.e: Ask directly about suicidal ideas — it does not increase risk; hopelessness, substance misuse and social isolation are further risks.

neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.s: A patient on fluoxetine is given tramadol and develops agitation, hyperthermia, sweating, tremor, hyperreflexia and clonus, worse in the legs. What is the management?
o: IV dantrolene as the first treatment
Stop the serotonergic drugs, give supportive care with benzodiazepines (cyproheptadine if severe)
neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.e: Serotonin syndrome develops within hours with hyperreflexia and clonus; neuroleptic malignant syndrome develops over days with rigidity and hyporeflexia.

neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.s: Three days after starting haloperidol, a patient has fever 40°C, lead-pipe rigidity, confusion, labile BP and CK 9,000 U/L. What is the management?
o: Stop the antipsychotic, cool and hydrate aggressively, and give dantrolene or bromocriptine in severe cases
neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.e: Complications include rhabdomyolysis with AKI and VTE; restart a different (atypical) antipsychotic cautiously after recovery.

neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.s: A 22-year-old man has 8 months of auditory hallucinations, delusions of control and social withdrawal. What is the first-line treatment?
o: An atypical antipsychotic (e.g., risperidone or olanzapine) with psychosocial support
neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.e: Clozapine is reserved for treatment resistance (failure of two antipsychotics), requiring FBC monitoring for agranulocytosis.

neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.s: A young man given IM haloperidol develops sustained painful upward deviation of the eyes and neck spasm. What is the immediate treatment?
neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.e: Acute dystonia (oculogyric crisis) occurs early; akathisia (propranolol), parkinsonism and late tardive dyskinesia are other EPSEs.

neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.s: A patient on lithium develops coarse tremor, vomiting, diarrhoea, ataxia and drowsiness after starting a diuretic. What is the most likely cause?
o: Lithium toxicity precipitated by thiazide-induced sodium depletion
neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.e: Lithium level, U&E and TFT monitoring; NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors and diuretics raise levels; haemodialysis for severe toxicity.

neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.s: A 26-year-old has recurrent unexpected episodes of palpitations, chest tightness, breathlessness and fear of dying lasting 10 minutes, with normal ECG and thyroid function. What is the best long-term management?
o: Cognitive behavioural therapy with an SSRI if needed
neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.e: Benzodiazepines risk dependence; exclude thyrotoxicosis, arrhythmia and phaeochromocytoma.

neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.s: A woman who survived an earthquake has 4 months of nightmares, flashbacks, hypervigilance and avoidance of reminders. What is the first-line treatment?
neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.e: Medication (SSRI/venlafaxine) is used if psychological therapy is declined, unavailable or insufficient.

neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.s: A 24-year-old has sudden inability to walk after a family dispute. Examination shows give-way weakness, positive Hoover's sign and normal reflexes; MRI is normal. What is the diagnosis and approach?
o: Functional neurological (conversion) disorder; explain the positive diagnosis and refer for physiotherapy/CBT
neurosciences-iii/psychiatry.e: Positive signs (Hoover's, inconsistency, distractibility) support diagnosis; avoid telling the patient "nothing is wrong".

neurosciences-iii/paediatrics.s: An 18-month-old has a 3-minute generalised seizure with fever 39.5°C from otitis media, recovering fully within 20 minutes. What is the appropriate management?
o: Treat the infection, give antipyretic advice and reassure parents; no antiepileptic drugs or EEG needed
neurosciences-iii/paediatrics.e: Simple febrile seizure: generalised, <15 min, once in 24 h, age 6 months–5 years; risk of later epilepsy is only slightly increased.
